title: Set active OpenCode tab dot on first user message
body:
## Goal

Guarantee that an interactive OpenCode root session shows the neutral active dot as soon as the first user message is submitted, and preserves it when OpenCode replaces the initial title with a descriptive title. Higher-priority state colors must still replace it normally.

## Evidence

- The observing session runs aidevops v3.32.112, which predates the terminal status controller. The latest released v3.32.141 already contains the neutral busy dot and preserves status across title updates.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-title-status.mjs:35-65` currently waits for a native `session.status` event before setting `busy`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-title-fallback.mjs:68-79` documents the existing first-user-message `message.updated` event shape, so the plugin can activate the dot at submission time without waiting for status timing.

## Implementation

- Extend `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-title-status.mjs` to map a `message.updated` event with `info.role === "user"` for the active interactive root session to `busy` when no permission request is pending.
- Keep permission yellow until answered; retain native retry red and idle green transitions.
- Update `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-title-status.mjs` with positive first-message coverage plus child, assistant, pending-permission, and headless regressions.
- Update `.agents/tools/terminal/terminal-title.md`, `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` to state that active indication starts on first submission.

## Hazards and compatibility

- Do not alter stored OpenCode session titles; status remains terminal-only.
- Preserve active-root filtering, headless opt-out, idempotent prefix replacement, and permission precedence.
- Duplicate user-message updates may call the status setter repeatedly, but the terminal title controller must continue suppressing identical rendered states.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-title-status.mjs`

- `npx --no-install biome check` on changed plugin files

- Pseudo-terminal OSC transition covering first user message to neutral active dot, descriptive title update, permission, retry, and idle.

## Acceptance criteria

- The first root-session user message sets the neutral active dot before any native `session.status` event.
- A later descriptive title update retains the neutral active dot.
- Permission, retry, and idle states replace the active dot with yellow, red, and green respectively.
- Assistant messages, child-session messages, malformed events, and headless sessions do not change terminal status.
- A user-message update cannot replace an unanswered permission indicator.

title: Fix incremental deployment convergence in linked worktrees and stale bundle environments
body:
## Objective

Make incremental release/update deployment converge on one coherent active runtime bundle when setup runs from a linked worktree or an existing AI session with a stale `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR`.

## Observed evidence

1. `setup.sh:_setup_run_ai_session_incremental` checks `[[ -d "$INSTALL_DIR/.git" ]]`. A linked worktree has a `.git` file, so `./setup.sh --stage ai-session` rejects the framework-mandated release worktree and falls back to full setup.
2. An OpenCode session inherited `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pointing at an older bundle. After the atomic agents stage activated v3.32.143, runtime-config reconciliation generated `subagent-index.toon` inside the older v3.32.141 bundle. Re-running with `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` unset correctly targeted the active `agents` symlink.
3. Incremental release deployment reported convergence while the active `agents` symlink still targeted v3.32.140. New releases updated the stale bundle's `VERSION`, causing both `aidevops --version` and `aidevops status` to claim v3.32.143/v3.32.144 even though the active bundle path and manifest were still v3.32.140.
4. Manually running the narrow `agents` and `runtime-config` stages from clean detached release worktrees atomically activated coherent v3.32.143 and then v3.32.144 bundles, proving the source bundles themselves were valid.

## Files and reference patterns

- `setup.sh`: `_setup_run_ai_session_incremental`, `_setup_ai_session_verify_deploy`, and scoped-stage dispatch.
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`: structural linked-worktree detection using `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `--git-common-dir`; reuse this pattern instead of testing whether `.git` is a directory.

title: Localdev proxy generation emits invalid Traefik routes and session-scoped certificates
body:
## What

Make generated localdev HTTPS proxy configuration valid on Traefik v3, remove an unused Docker-provider dependency, and ensure mkcert uses a stable CA root rather than OpenCode's session-isolated data directory.

## Evidence

- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-routes.sh:50` emits `Host(`base.local`) || Host(`*.base.local`)`. Traefik v3.3 rejects the wildcard as an invalid HostSNI hostname and omits the router. Replacing the base rule with exact `Host(`base.local`)` immediately restored the router; branch routes are already emitted as exact hosts by `localdev-helper-branch.sh:156`.
- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-init.sh:402-404,449-450` enables the Docker provider and mounts the Docker socket even though localdev creates file-provider routes. With a current Docker engine this generated repeated API 1.24/minimum 1.40 errors; the Traefik API reported zero Docker-provider routers. Removing the provider and socket mount cleared the errors while file routes remained enabled.
- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-ports.sh:359` invokes mkcert with inherited `XDG_DATA_HOME`. OpenCode intentionally isolates that variable per session, so mkcert creates a new session-scoped CA and resulting certificates fail system trust verification. Invoking mkcert without inherited `CAROOT`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` selects its stable platform location.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-routes.sh`: emit only the exact base-domain rule; retain exact branch routes as the subdomain mechanism.
- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-init.sh`: make new static/Compose templates file-provider-only and provide a stable mkcert invocation path independent of runtime XDG isolation.
- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-ports.sh`: generate certificates through the stable mkcert wrapper.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-localdev-helper-config.sh` (new): characterize generated route, proxy templates, and mkcert environment behavior.

### Complete Write Surface

Callers are `localdev-helper.sh init`, `add`, and branch registration. Outputs are `~/.local-dev-proxy/traefik.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `conf.d/*.yml`, and `~/.local-ssl-certs/*`. Existing user configurations must not be destructively rewritten; this change governs newly generated files and explicit init/add operations.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Preserve exact branch-domain routing; do not replace it with a broad wildcard matcher.
- Do not remove custom Docker-provider configuration from existing installations automatically.
- Keep mkcert's normal platform default and explicit user `CAROOT` override semantics available while preventing runtime-only `XDG_DATA_HOME` from changing the CA unexpectedly.
- Trust-store installation can require administrator authority; surface a clear actionable failure instead of exposing or copying CA private keys.

### Verification Before Dispatch

1. Run the new focused localdev config test.
2. Run `shellcheck` on the three modified helpers and test.
3. Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` for the changed-file gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated base routes load in Traefik v3 without wildcard HostSNI errors, while exact branch routes remain supported.
- New localdev proxy templates use only the file provider and do not mount the Docker socket.
- Certificate generation is deterministic across isolated OpenCode sessions and does not silently create a new CA under session-scoped `XDG_DATA_HOME`.
- Focused regression tests cover positive generation and the negative regressions above.

title: Prevent pre-edit tool timeout from creating unreported duplicate worktrees
body:
## Context

Calling the OpenCode `aidevops_pre_edit_check` tool from canonical `main` with a code-task description returned `Pre-edit check exit 1: STOP` plus only the initial `LOOP-AUTO: Code task detected, worktree required` line. The underlying loop-mode script nevertheless created `bugfix/gh28074-issue-28074-reduce-shell-environment-com` in a linked worktree, but the tool never returned its path. The interactive session therefore followed the reported STOP guidance and created a second worktree manually. The unreported worktree remained registered and cleanup-safe removal was blocked by ownership checks.

## Likely cause

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs:createPreEditCheckTool` gives `pre-edit-check.sh --loop-mode` a fixed 10-second timeout and maps a timeout with no status to exit 1. Loop-mode worktree creation can exceed 10 seconds; the child helper can complete after the parent tool times out, leaving a successful side effect reported as STOP.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs`

- A loop-mode pre-edit tool call cannot create an unreported linked worktree.
- Successful auto-creation returns the exact created path and actionable next step.
- Timeouts are classified explicitly rather than rewritten as ordinary exit 1.
- Timeout recovery either waits safely, terminates the complete child process tree before side effects complete, or reconciles and reports a worktree created after timeout.
- Repeating the call does not create a duplicate branch/worktree.

title: Worktree remove fails silently when a live cwd blocks cleanup
body:
## What

Make manual `worktree-helper.sh remove` failures explain why cleanup was refused when a live process has its current directory inside the target worktree.

## Evidence

- A clean, merged worktree had a dead ownership-registry PID but still hosted a local GUI process whose cwd was inside the worktree.
- `worktree-helper.sh remove <path>` correctly exited non-zero and preserved the worktree, but emitted no stdout/stderr. The only evidence was an `active-cwd` row in `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log`.
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:255-259` logs `active-cwd` and returns `1` without exposing the reason to an interactive caller.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh:108-115,244-255` propagates that return without printing a diagnostic.

Silent refusal makes safe cleanup look like a no-op and encourages repeated removal attempts or unsafe process termination. The guard itself behaved correctly; this task is diagnostic propagation only.

## How

### Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: expose a machine-readable guard reason without weakening the fail-closed decision or logging contract.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh`: for explicit manual removal, print the target, safe reason, and recovery guidance when the shared guard refuses removal.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit.sh` and/or a focused `worktree-helper remove` test: cover visible `current-worktree`, `active-cwd`, canonical, and ownership refusal messages.

### Constraints

- Preserve the non-overridable live-cwd guard; `--force` must still not bypass it.
- Do not expose process command lines, environment variables, repository-private names, or file contents in diagnostics.
- Keep background cleanup noise bounded; only explicit/manual callers need user-facing output unless a caller opts in.
- Keep Bash 3.2 compatibility, explicit function returns, and ShellCheck zero findings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current-worktree and canonical refusals are similarly visible without duplicate messages.
- [ ] Audit rows remain exactly once per refusal.

title: bundle-helper.sh resolve mutates canonical checkouts via _write_cached_detection
body:
## Description

`bundle-helper.sh resolve` calls `_write_cached_detection` which writes `detected_bundle` and `detected_bundle_at` directly into the project's `.aidevops.json` on the canonical checkout. This mutates automation-read-only canonical repos, leaving them dirty (uncommitted changes).

The mutation happens as a side-effect of reading bundle config during worker dispatch. It is a cache write intended to speed up subsequent `resolve` calls by avoiding marker-file re-scans, but on canonical checkouts this write leaves the repo with a modified tracked file and no commit.

## Expected Behavior

Bundle detection cache must not mutate canonical human checkouts. Canonical repos must remain byte-identical regardless of which automation paths read their config.

If a cache is needed, the framework should use a user-local path outside the checkout (e.g., `~/.aidevops/cache/bundle/<repo-slug>.json`), not modify project files in-place.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
git -C /home/ubuntu/Git/ans_playbooks status --porcelain
```

**Actual output**:

```
 M .aidevops.json
```

**Diff**:

```diff
-  "plugins": []
+  "plugins": [],
+  "detected_bundle": "agent,infrastructure",
+  "detected_bundle_at": "2026-07-17T00:07:02Z"
```

**Expected output**: (empty — no uncommitted changes)

**Causal code**:

```bash
git blame bundle-helper.sh -L 165,210
```

`_write_cached_detection()` at bundle-helper.sh:170 blindly merges `detected_bundle` and `detected_bundle_at` into the project's `.aidevops.json` with no check for whether this is a canonical checkout.

**Call-site sweep**:

```
bundle-helper.sh:344     _write_cached_detection "$project_path" "$comma_separated"    # in _run_bundle_detection
pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:345  "$bundle_helper" resolve "$repo_path"             # caller via resolve
pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:280  "$bundle_helper" get model_defaults.implementation "$repo_path"  # get also triggers resolve
testing-setup-helper.sh:547          bundle_json=$("${SCRIPT_DIR}/bundle-helper.sh" resolve "$project_dir")  # same pattern
```

## Root Cause

`_write_cached_detection()` (bundle-helper.sh:170-210) is designed as a performance cache for bundle marker detection. It writes to the project directory because bundle detection is conceptually per-project. However, there is no architectural distinction between a canonical checkout (which must remain read-only) and an automation workspace (where writes are expected).

PR #27439 and GH#27155 established that all automation writes must use:
- Fenced automation workspaces (not human checkouts), or
- User-local cache directories

`_write_cached_detection` was not migrated as part of that work. It was also not caught by the byte-identity assertions added to `test-canonical-readonly-diagnostics.sh` because those tests only cover `pulse_canonical_recover`, not `bundle-helper.sh`.

All three call sites (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `testing-setup-helper.sh`, and direct CLI use) trigger mutation of the canonical checkout.

## Recommended Fix

1. Move `_write_cached_detection` output to `~/.aidevops/cache/bundle/<slug>.json` (or compute a deterministic key from the repo path) so it persists across sessions without touching project files.
2. `_read_cached_detection` falls back to the user-local cache, then to marker-file scan.
3. The project-local `.aidevops.json` `detected_bundle` field remains optional — used only if explicitly committed by the user or set via `repos.json`.

Alternatively, add an explicit canonical-checkout check before writing:

```bash
if _is_canonical_checkout "$project_path"; then
    _log "skipping bundle cache write: $project_path is a canonical checkout"
    return 0
fi
```

## Acceptence Criteria

- `bundle-helper.sh resolve` (and `detect`, `get`, `show`) never modifies `.aidevops.json` on a canonical checkout.
- Bundle detection results are cached per-session or in `~/.aidevops/cache/bundle/` and survive framework restarts.
- Canonical repos remain byte-identical before and after any bundle-helper call.
- Existing bundle resolution behavior (resolution priority chain, marker matching, compose) is unchanged for non-canonical workspaces.
- Existing tests continue to pass; new tests assert canonical byte-identity for each resolved bundle path.

## Workarounds Applied

- `git restore .aidevops.json` via Python file-write bypass (canonical git guard blocks `git checkout`/`git restore` on canonical repos) — repeated whenever the bundle cache fires.
- Dismissed `canonical-recovery-*.advisory` files generated by pulse after bundle cache dirtied the repo.
- No automation exists to revert this mutation — the `git-pull-canonical.sh` timer pulls but cannot revert because the pull itself is a fast-forward that doesn't touch `detected_bundle`.

## Siblings

None yet. The relate issue #27977 addresses a different mutation path (TODO.md reconciliation by issue-sync-helper.sh).

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.145
- Runtime: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- GH#27155 / PR #27439 established automation-read-only human canonical checkouts.
- Issue #27977 documents a separate canonical mutation via `sync_todo_refs_for_repo`.
- The `detected_bundle` field was introduced by t2565 (original bundle detection implementation) before the canonical-read-only policy was established.

title: OpenCode plugin pinned to stale runtime bundle after ~/.aidevops/agents symlink update
body:
## Description

The OpenCode aidevops plugin resolves `~/.aidevops/agents` to the active runtime bundle path ONCE at module load time via `realpathSync()` in `index.mjs:73-79`. If the `~/.aidevops/agents` symlink is updated while OpenCode is running (e.g., by `aidevops update`, release deployment, or automated bundle deploy), the plugin remains pinned to the stale bundle for the rest of the session.

This causes:
- All child shell processes get the old `scriptsDir` prepended to PATH
- `gh` resolves to the old bundle's shim — the fix from GH#27804 (`PRIVACY_GH_BIN="$REAL_GH" privacy_is_target_public`) exists in bundles >= 3.32.138 but never reaches the session
- Every framework feature that depends on the active bundle path (tools, hooks, environment injection) runs from the stale version
- The user must restart OpenCode to pick up the new bundle, even though the symlink has been pointing at it for hours

## Expected Behavior

The plugin should re-resolve `~/.aidevops/agents` periodically or detect symlink changes so that shell subprocesses use the current active bundle. A session that starts on bundle X should not be permanently pinned to X when the system symlink has been updated to Y.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
printenv AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR
which gh
type gh
```

**Actual output**:

```
/home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.121-.../agents
/home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.121-.../agents/scripts/gh
gh is /home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.121-.../agents/scripts/gh
```

**Expected output**: (should show the path of the actually active bundle — 3.32.145 in this case)

```
/home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.145-.../agents
/home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.145-.../agents/scripts/gh
```

**Symptom command 2**:

```bash
readlink ~/.aidevops/agents
```

**Actual output 2**: (at the SAME time as the above)

```
/home/ubuntu/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.32.145-.../agents
```

The symlink already points to the new bundle, but the plugin is pinned to the old one.

**Causal code**:

```javascript
// index.mjs:73-79 — resolves ONCE at module load time
const AGENTS_DIR = (() => {
  try {
    return realpathSync(ACTIVE_AGENTS_DIR);  // ← pinned at process start
  } catch {
    return ACTIVE_AGENTS_DIR;
  }
})();
```

The result is used for the entire process lifetime:
- `index.mjs:254` — `scriptsDir: SCRIPTS_DIR` (from `AGENTS_DIR`)
- `shell-env.mjs:121-125` — injects `scriptsDir` into every spawned shell's PATH
- All other hooks that consume `AGENTS_DIR`, `SCRIPTS_DIR`, etc.

**Call-site sweep**:

```
index.mjs:73-79     AGENTS_DIR = realpathSync(ACTIVE_AGENTS_DIR)  — once at module init
index.mjs:251-256   createShellEnvHook({ agentsDir: AGENTS_DIR, scriptsDir: SCRIPTS_DIR })
shell-env.mjs:121-125  output.env.PATH = [scriptsDir, ...pathParts]  — per shell spawn
shell-env.mjs:129      output.env.AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR = agentsDir   — per shell spawn
```

## Root Cause

The plugin uses module-level `const` for `AGENTS_DIR`, `SCRIPTS_DIR`, and other derived paths. These are computed once when the module is first imported. Node.js caches the module, so subsequent hook invocations (which happen on every shell spawn and every tool execution) all use the stale value.

The `shell-env.mjs` hook faithfully injects `scriptsDir` into every spawned shell, but that `scriptsDir` is the stale one from module load time.

## Recommended Fix

**Option A — Re-resolve at each shell spawn**: Replace the module-level `realpathSync` with a lazy getter that re-resolves on each shell-env hook invocation:

```javascript
// In shell-env.mjs hook, instead of using scriptsDir closure:
const resolvedAgentsDir = realpathSync(activeAgentsDir);
const resolvedScriptsDir = join(resolvedAgentsDir, "scripts");
if (existsSync(resolvedScriptsDir)) {
  const pathParts = currentPath.split(":").filter(...);
  output.env.PATH = [resolvedScriptsDir, ...pathParts].join(":");
}
```

Trade-off: re-resolves on every shell spawn (~100µs stat call). Slight cost but negligible for shell spawn frequency.

**Option B — Periodic stat-based invalidation**: Keep the module-level `AGENTS_DIR` but add a stat-based TTL (e.g., 60s) that re-resolves when the symlink's mtime changes:

```javascript
let _agentsDirCache = { path: "", mtime: 0 };
function resolveAgentsDir() {
  const stat = fs.lstatSync(ACTIVE_AGENTS_DIR);
  if (stat.mtimeMs !== _agentsDirCache.mtime) {
    _agentsDirCache = { path: realpathSync(ACTIVE_AGENTS_DIR), mtime: stat.mtimeMs };
  }
  return _agentsDirCache.path;
}
```

Trade-off: 2 stats per call + 1 realpath on change. More robust for long-running sessions.

**Option C — fs.watch on the symlink**: Watch `~/.aidevops/agents` for change events and update the cached path. Trade-off: event-based, but adds complexity for process lifecycle and cleanup.

## Acceptence Criteria

- If `~/.aidevops/agents` symlink is updated while OpenCode is running, subsequently spawned shells get the new bundle's `scripts/` directory on PATH.
- `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` env var in child shells reflects the current active bundle, not the one at session start.
- `gh`, `git`, and other PATH shims resolve to the current active bundle version.
- No regression for normal startup (symlink unchanged during session — single resolution).
- Existing tests continue to pass.

## Workarounds Applied

- None available for a long-running OpenCode session. The user must restart OpenCode (`/new` or close/reopen) to see the new bundle.

## Siblings

This issue was discovered while investigating GH#27804 (gh shim privacy scan recursion). The fix for #27804 exists in bundles >= 3.32.138 but was invisible because the session was pinned to 3.32.121 by this stale-resolution bug.

See-also: #28073 (incremental deployment convergence — related but scoped to setup/deploy, not plugin)

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.32.145 (active symlink), but session pinned to 3.32.121
- Runtime: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## What

The pulse deterministic merge pass has had **5 consecutive cycles** with eligible-unmerged PRs but zero merges. The threshold is `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.

## Why

Eligible-unmerged means `APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review`. When this is non-zero AND the merge count is zero across multiple cycles, the merge pass is structurally blocked — gates failing closed (e.g. branch-protection 404 mis-fire), GraphQL exhaustion, repo-allowlist mismatch, or a regression in the merge gates themselves.

## How

### Files Scope

Investigation only — no `Files Scope` declared.

### Snapshot

```
eligible_unmerged_this_cycle=2, eligible_stuck_count=2, zero_progress_cycles=5
```

### Investigation steps

1. Read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the meta-issue was filed (`grep 'Merge pass: skipping' `) — the per-PR skip reason is logged for every cycle.
2. Cross-check `pulse-stats.json` for circuit-breaker fires and the `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` counter — if non-zero, the t2922 fail-closed path is mis-firing.
3. Reproduce the merge gate decision for one stuck PR via `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` — it explains what the pulse decided and why.
4. Apply the fix (often a one-line gate adjustment) and verify the next cycle drops zero-progress to 0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause of the throughput collapse identified.
- [ ] At least one of the stuck PRs successfully auto-merges.
- [ ] `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` reads 0 in `pulse-stats.json`.

Filed automatically by `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (t3193). The detector resets the zero-progress counter on any successful merge — if the meta-issue is stale (cause already resolved), close it manually.

title: bug: pulse-check systemd ExecStart quoting double-escape causes daily exit 127
body:
## Summary

`aidevops-pulse-check.service` systemd user unit has a quoting bug in `ExecStart` that causes daily failure with exit code 127 (command not found). The `pulse-check` timer has been failing every day since at least Jul 13.

## Symptom

```
$ systemctl --user status aidevops-pulse-check.service
× aidevops-pulse-check.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=127/n/a
× aidevops-pulse-check.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.

$ journalctl --user -u aidevops-pulse-check.service -n 5
Jul 17 06:20:00 devvm systemd[1334]: Starting aidevops-pulse-check.service...
Jul 17 06:20:00 devvm systemd[1334]: ...Main process exited, code=exited, status=127/n/a
Jul 17 06:20:00 devvm systemd[1334]: ...Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Jul 17 06:20:00 devvm systemd[1334]: Failed to start aidevops-pulse-check.service.
```

## Service file (broken)

```
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc '"<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply"'
```

## Root cause

The `ExecStart` has **double-wrapped quoting**: single quotes at the systemd level (correct for grouping) with double quotes INSIDE the bash `-c` string. This causes bash to interpret the entire `"path/to/script.sh apply"` as a single double-quoted word, making it look for an executable file named with a literal space:

```bash
# What systemd passes to bash -c:
"<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply"

# How bash interprets it:
# Double quotes → one WORD (space does not split)
# Command = "<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply" (with space in filename)
# → exit 127: No such file or directory
```

## Reproducer

```bash
# BROKEN: double quotes inside the -c string
$ bash -lc '"/usr/bin/true bogus"'
bash: line 1: /usr/bin/true bogus: No such file or directory
$ echo $?
127

# CORRECT: inner quotes removed
$ bash -lc '/usr/bin/true bogus'
# (no output, exit 0)
```

Confirmed with the actual pulse-check script:

```bash
$ bash -lc '"<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply"'
bash: line 1: <HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply: No such file or directory
$ echo $?
127
```

## Comparison with working services

Other services generated by `_systemd_escape` (in `_install_scheduler_systemd`) use `\"` escaping within double-quoted systemd blocks and work correctly:

```ini
# CORRECT (from aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service)
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc "\"<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh\""

# CORRECT (from aidevops-pulse-merge.service)
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc "\"<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh\" run"
```

The `_systemd_escape()` function at `schedulers-linux.sh:66` correctly produces `\"...\"` quoting. The pulse-check service was NOT generated by `_install_scheduler_systemd` — it was generated by a code path that used `printf '%q'` (now in `routine-helper.sh:438`) or raw `'\"...\"'` string interpolation (used in `auto-update-helper.sh:973` and several other service generators).

## Impact

- `aidevops-pulse-check.service` fails daily at 06:20 since Jul 13 2026
- Pulse check findings are never filed unless the service is fixed or the helper runs manually
- **Other services using the `'\"...\"'` pattern are also at risk** if the command string has the script path AND argument inside the inner double quotes rather than as separate unquoted tokens

## Call sites at risk

The following ExecStart generators produce systemd `ExecStart=` values that could suffer from similar quoting bugs:

| File | Line | Pattern | Risk |
|------|------|---------|------|
| `routine-helper.sh` | 438 | `printf '%q' "$command"` | **High** — `printf '%q'` produces shell-safe quoting, not systemd-safe quoting; double-escapes if command contains quotes |
| `auto-update-helper.sh` | 973 | `'\"${script_path}\" check'` | **Low** — individual component quoting, args outside quotes |
| `repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh` | 1059 | `'\"${script_path}\" check'` | **Low** — same pattern |
| `repo-sync-helper.sh` | 809 | `'\"${script_path}\" check'` | **Low** — same pattern |
| `worker-watchdog-cmd.sh` | 537 | `'${script_path} --check'` | **Low** — no inner quotes |
| `auto-update-helper-scheduler.sh` | 273 | `'${script_path} check'` | **Low** — no inner quotes |

## Suggested fix

**For `schedulers-linux.sh` (already correct)**: No change needed — `_systemd_escape()` produces correct `\"...\"` quoting for ExecStart.

**For `routine-helper.sh:438`**: Replace `printf '%q'` with `_systemd_escape()` for systemd unit generation to produce consistent quoting:

```bash
# Current (broken for commands with arguments):
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc $(printf '%q' "$command")

# Fixed:
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc $(_systemd_escape "$command")
```

**For `auto-update-helper.sh:973` and similar hardcoded templates**: These work for their specific patterns but are fragile. Consider refactoring to use `_systemd_escape()` for consistency.

**For the broken service on disk**: Regenerate the service by either:
1. Re-running the scheduler setup (if `setup/install-schedulers.sh` covers pulse-check)
2. Manually correcting `ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc '<HOME>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply'` (remove inner double quotes)

## Verification

After fix:
```bash
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start aidevops-pulse-check.service
systemctl --user status aidevops-pulse-check.service  # should show active/exited with exit-code 0
journalctl --user -u aidevops-pulse-check.service -n 10  # verify no 127 errors
```

title: bug: approval-snapshot-v2.sh Argument list too long with --argjson comments for high-comment issues
body:
## Description

`approval-snapshot-v2.sh` passes large JSON payloads (`$comments_json`, `$linked_references_json`) to `jq` via `--argjson`, which places them in the process argv. When an issue has many comments (pulse dispatch cycles, review feedback threads), the combined argv exceeds `ARG_MAX` (~2MB on Linux), causing `jq` to fail with "Argument list too long".

This prevents `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <repo>` from completing for issues with a large comment history.

## Expected Behavior

`sudo aidevops approve issue` should succeed regardless of comment count. Large JSON payloads should be passed to `jq` via stdin, temp files with `--slurpfile`, or another method that avoids argv limits.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
sudo /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/aidevops approve issue 1748 <org>/<private-repo>
```

**Actual output**:

```
Type APPROVE to confirm: APPROVE
/home/ubuntu/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh: line 167: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long
[ERROR] Could not build the immutable approval snapshot; approval was not posted
```

**Expected output**:

Approval comment posted successfully, issue approved.

**Causal code**:

Line 166-168 of `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` (commit `ecbccca6ff`):

```
jq -cS -n --arg repo "$normalized_slug" --arg empty "$empty_string" \
  --arg issue_kind "$APPROVAL_TARGET_ISSUE" --argjson number "$target_number" \
  --argjson issue "$issue_json" --argjson comments "$comments_json" \
  --argjson linked_references "$linked_references_json" '{...}'
```

The same pattern occurs at lines 196-198 (PR branch) with 6 large JSON payloads via argv, making it even more vulnerable.

**Call-site sweep** (all `--argjson` + large variable in approval-snapshot-v2.sh):

- Line 167: `--argjson issue "$issue_json" --argjson comments "$comments_json"`
- Line 168: `--argjson linked_references "$linked_references_json"`
- Lines 196-198: PR variant with `--argjson issue "$issue_json" --argjson pr "$pr_json" --argjson comments "$comments_json" --argjson review_comments "$review_comments_json" --argjson reviews "$reviews_json" --argjson linked_references "$linked_references_json"`

Related files with same pattern:
- `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:162` — `--argjson comments "$comments"`
- `dispatch-claim-helper.sh:577,651` — `--argjson comments "$comments_json"`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find an issue with a large comment count (50+ comments, e.g., from pulse dispatch cycles)
2. Run `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <owner/repo>`
3. Confirm with `APPROVE`
4. Observe `/usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long` error

## Workarounds Applied

- Documented the bug in `~/bug2.txt` with analysis
- Issue #1748 (<org>/<private-repo>) could not be approved via standard flow
- Created `approve-nmr-issues.sh` to batch-approve, but this bug blocks it for high-comment issues

## Proposed Fix

Replace `--argjson comments "$comments_json"` with a method that avoids argv:

**Option A (temp file + --slurpfile)**:
```
comments_file=$(mktemp)
printf '%s' "$comments_json" > "$comments_file"
jq -cS -n --slurpfile comments "$comments_file" ...
rm -f "$comments_file"
```

**Option B (stdin pipe)**:
```
printf '%s' "$comments_json" | jq -cS -n \
  --arg repo "$normalized_slug" \
  --argjson issue "$issue_json" \
  --argjson linked_references "$linked_references_json" \
  'input as $comments | {...}'
```

Option A is preferred as `--slurpfile` is designed for large payloads that would exceed argv limits.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.145
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

title: bug(pr-review-thread-response-scanner): escalation fires after 3 attempts even when worker pushed commits — missing last_head_sha in state
body:
## Description

`pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` escalates to `maintainer_attention=true` after `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_ESCALATE_AFTER=3` (default) attempts when the thread fingerprint is unchanged across dispatch cycles. This criterion is incorrect when the worker fixed code and pushed a commit between attempts — reviewers give inline threads but do not close them; threads remain open with the same PRRT IDs until the reviewer re-reviews after the fix. The escalation fires based on unchanged thread IDs even though real commits were pushed and the PR is making progress.

## Expected Behavior

Escalation should only fire when the worker has attempted a fix *without producing any new commit* on the PR branch across N consecutive dispatches. A new commit (headRefOid change) since the last dispatch proves the worker made progress; the attempt counter should reset regardless of thread fingerprint state.

## Reproducer

**Symptom observed** (from `~/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log`):

```
[2026-07-15T03:43:22Z] dispatch: Majowka/mesh-manager#2641 not launching response worker —
  same unresolved thread fingerprint reached attempt 25; maintainer attention recommended
[2026-07-15T07:13:51Z] dispatch: Majowka/mesh-manager#2641 not launching response worker —
  same unresolved thread fingerprint reached attempt 28
```

State file for PR #2641 (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/pr-review-thread-response/Majowka-mesh-manager-2641.state`):
```
fingerprint=PRRT_kwDOPhWWNs6Qc30C:...,PRRT_kwDOPhWWNs6QjK-Q:...   # 31 thread IDs
dispatched_at=1784099631
thread_count=31
attempt_count=28
maintainer_attention=true
attention_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint
```

No `last_head_sha` field. Whether any of the 28 workers pushed commits is unknown — the state file does not record the PR branch SHA at dispatch time, so commit-level progress is invisible to the escalation logic.

**Root review model that exposes the bug:** Reviewer submits CHANGES_REQUESTED with inline threads (PRRT IDs). Worker reads threads, fixes code, pushes commit, resolves threads via `scanner.sh resolve`. Reviewer re-reviews; if satisfied, approves. Between the worker's commit push and the reviewer's re-review, threads remain open with the same PRRT IDs — fingerprint appears unchanged even though code was fixed and committed.

**Causal code** (all in `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`):

```
Line 39:  PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_ESCALATE_AFTER="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_ESCALATE_AFTER:-3}"

Line 109: _prrts_should_escalate_attempt() {
Line 116:   [[ "$threshold" -gt 0 && "$repeated_same_fingerprint" == "$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE"
             && "$attempt_count" -ge "$threshold" ]]
          # No check for head SHA change — same PRRT IDs treated as "stuck"
          # even when worker pushed a commit

Line 340: gh pr list ... --json number,title,isDraft,labels,headRefName,author
          # headRefName = branch name only; headRefOid (commit SHA) is NOT fetched

Line 778: if [[ -n "$last_fingerprint" && "$fingerprint" == "$last_fingerprint" ]]; then
Line 779:     state_repeated_same_fingerprint="$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE"
Line 780:     next_attempt_count=$((last_attempt_count + 1))
          # Counter increments on same fingerprint with no SHA comparison

Line 809: _prrts_write_state() {
Line 822:   printf 'fingerprint=%s\n' "$fingerprint"
Line 823:   printf 'dispatched_at=%s\n' "$now_epoch"
Line 824:   printf 'thread_count=%s\n' "$thread_count"
Line 825:   printf 'attempt_count=%s\n' "$attempt_count"
          # last_head_sha not persisted
```

**Call-site sweep — all locations requiring change:**

```
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:340  — _prrts_list_open_prs: add headRefOid to --json fields
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:490  — _prrts_scan_repo_to_files loop: extract head_oid from row
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:517  — candidates file columns: thread head_oid through
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:721  — _prrts_read_state: add last_head_sha output var
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:778  — _prrts_should_dispatch: compare current vs saved SHA, reset counter on mismatch
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:809  — _prrts_write_state: add last_head_sha param + persist
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:109  — _prrts_should_escalate_attempt: require same_head_sha in addition to same_fingerprint
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:1054 — _prrts_maybe_dispatch_pr call-site: pass head_oid
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. PR has CHANGES_REQUESTED with inline review threads (PRRT IDs A, B, C)
2. Scanner dispatches worker → worker fixes code, pushes commit, resolves some threads
3. Remaining threads stay open (reviewer must re-review before closing or approving)
4. Next dispatch cycle: fingerprint = same PRRT IDs → `same_fingerprint=true`, `attempt_count++`
5. After 3 cycles: `_prrts_should_escalate_attempt` fires → `maintainer_attention=true`, dispatch stops
6. PR was making real progress (commits pushed) but is now permanently blocked from worker help

## Proposed Fix

**1. Fetch `headRefOid` in `_prrts_list_open_prs` (line 340):**
```bash
gh pr list ... --json number,title,isDraft,labels,headRefName,headRefOid,author
```

**2. Persist `last_head_sha` in `_prrts_write_state` (line 809):**
```bash
printf 'last_head_sha=%s\n' "$head_sha"
```

**3. Read it back in `_prrts_read_state` (line 721).**

**4. Reset counter in `_prrts_should_dispatch` (line 778) when SHA changed:**
```bash
if [[ -n "$last_fingerprint" && "$fingerprint" == "$last_fingerprint" ]]; then
    if [[ -n "$last_head_sha" && "$current_head_sha" != "$last_head_sha" ]]; then
        # Worker pushed a commit — real progress, reset counter
        state_repeated_same_fingerprint="$PRRTS_BOOL_FALSE"
        next_attempt_count=1
    else
        state_repeated_same_fingerprint="$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE"
        next_attempt_count=$((last_attempt_count + 1))
    fi
fi
```

**5. Tighten escalation condition (line 116) to require both same fingerprint AND same SHA:**
```bash
[[ "$threshold" -gt 0 \
   && "$repeated_same_fingerprint" == "$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE" \
   && "$same_head_sha" == "$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE" \
   && "$attempt_count" -ge "$threshold" ]]
```

## Workarounds Applied

None. Bug discovered through log analysis during pulse merge investigation session.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.145
- **Latest version**: 3.32.145
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: mesh-manager (develop)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- Affected PRs (live evidence): Majowka/mesh-manager#2641 (28 attempts, 31 threads), Majowka/mesh-manager#2647 (9 attempts, 2 threads)
- Related closed issues: GH#26124 (worker success/failure distinction — `analysis_complete` field), GH#25889 (escalation hardening, PR#25898). Neither addressed the commit-progress blind spot.
- `headRefOid` is queryable from the same `gh pr list` call — adding it to `--json` at line 340 is the only external API change needed.

title: Bug: reject temporary OpenCode binaries when generating stable launcher shim
body:
## Task

Prevent aidevops setup from generating `~/.local/bin/opencode` shims that pin OpenCode to an executable inside an operating-system temporary directory.

## Why

An interactive setup run selected a valid NVM-hosted OpenCode executable under macOS `/var/folders/.../T/tmp...`. The generated shim stored that absolute path. After the temporary tree was removed, every `opencode` invocation failed before startup even though a durable Homebrew installation remained available.

## How

- Add temporary-path classification beside `_setup_opencode_node_path_for_binary` in both setup implementations.
- Resolve each candidate with `command -v` before validation.
- Skip candidates under `TMPDIR`, Linux temporary roots, and macOS `/var/folders/.../T` roots.
- Preserve the existing durable candidate order and validation behavior.
- Add focused regression coverage for positive temporary-path detection, durable-path acceptance, durable fallback selection, and rejection of temporary PATH entries.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh:170-250` — setup service implementation.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh:2166-2248` — bootstrap/tool-install mirror.
- `tests/test-opencode-stable-shim.sh` — focused regression test.

## Complete Write Surface

- Callers/readers: `_setup_find_valid_opencode_binary` in both setup implementations.
- Writers: `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` writes `~/.local/bin/opencode`; no schema or migration applies.
- Tests: new focused shell regression test sources `_services.sh`; both mirrored implementations receive the same change.
- Generated/deployed mirrors: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh` and `.agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh` are both source surfaces and must remain behaviorally aligned.
- Cleanup/rollback: reverting the candidate filter restores prior selection behavior; existing durable shims remain valid.

## Hazards and Compatibility

- Preserve Homebrew, Linuxbrew, user npm, Bun, and durable NVM installations.
- Resolve relative PATH candidates before classifying them so a temporary executable cannot bypass the filter as bare `opencode`.
- If no durable candidate exists, retain the existing failure/install path rather than persisting a path known to disappear.
- No concurrency, migration-order, or mixed-version state hazard applies; selection remains idempotent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A preferred executable under `TMPDIR` or macOS `/var/folders/.../T` is never validated or written into the stable shim.
- A durable known candidate is selected when the preferred candidate is temporary.
- A bare `opencode` resolving to a temporary PATH entry is rejected.
- Existing durable paths, including Homebrew and user NVM paths, remain accepted.
- Focused tests, ShellCheck, `git diff --check`, and changed-file local linters pass.

## Verification Before Dispatch

```bash

.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh

```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `_status_runtime_bundle_integrity` and `_status_active_bundle_version` functions can be made more robust against unset or empty `HOME` and unresolved paths. Currently, if `HOME` is unset, referencing `${HOME}` directly will trigger an unbound variable error under `set -u`. Additionally, when defining paths relative to `HOME`, we should use the `${HOME:+$HOME/relative/path}` pattern instead of `${HOME:-}/relative/path` to prevent resolving to root-level paths (like `/.aidevops/...`) when `HOME` is unset or empty, avoiding potential permission issues or unintended behavior.

```shell
_status_active_bundle_version() {
	local active_version="${HOME:+$HOME/.aidevops/agents/VERSION}"
	if [[ -n "$active_version" && -r "$active_version" ]]; then
		tr -d '[:space:]' <"$active_version"
		return 0
	fi
	get_version
	return 0
}

_status_runtime_bundle_integrity() {
	local active_link="${HOME:+$HOME/.aidevops/agents}"
	if [[ -z "$active_link" ]]; then
		print_warning "Active runtime bundle mismatch: HOME is not set"
		return 0
	fi

	local active_root=""
	local bundles_root=""
	local manifest_file=""
	local active_version=""
	local manifest_status=""
	local manifest_version=""
	local manifest_sha=""
	local deployed_sha=""

	if [[ ! -L "$active_link" ]]; then
		print_warning "Active runtime bundle mismatch: agents path is not an activation symlink"
		return 0
	fi
	active_root=$(cd "$active_link" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || active_root=""
	local bundles_dir="${HOME:+$HOME/.aidevops/runtime-bundles}"
	bundles_root=$(cd "${bundles_dir:-}" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || bundles_root=""
	if [[ -z "$active_root" || -z "$bundles_root" ]]; then
		print_warning "Active runtime bundle mismatch: target=${active_root:-missing}, status=missing, VERSION=missing, manifest version=missing, manifest SHA=missing, deployed SHA=missing"
		return 0
	fi
	manifest_file="$active_root/.bundle-manifest"
	[[ -r "$active_root/VERSION" ]] && active_version=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$active_root/VERSION" 2>/dev/null) || active_version=""
	[[ -r "$manifest_file" ]] && manifest_status=$(_status_bundle_manifest_value "$manifest_file" status) || manifest_status=""
	[[ -r "$manifest_file" ]] && manifest_version=$(_status_bundle_manifest_value "$manifest_file" framework_version) || manifest_version=""
	[[ -r "$manifest_file" ]] && manifest_sha=$(_status_bundle_manifest_value "$manifest_file" git_sha) || manifest_sha=""
	local deployed_sha_file="${HOME:+$HOME/.aidevops/.deployed-sha}"
	[[ -n "$deployed_sha_file" && -r "$deployed_sha_file" ]] && deployed_sha=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$deployed_sha_file" 2>/dev/null) || deployed_sha=""

	if [[ "$active_root" != "$bundles_root/"*/agents || "$manifest_status" != "validated" ||
		-z "$active_version" || -z "$manifest_version" || -z "$manifest_sha" || -z "$deployed_sha" ||
		"$active_version" != "$manifest_version" || "$manifest_sha" != "$deployed_sha" ]]; then
		print_warning "Active runtime bundle mismatch: target=${active_root:-missing}, status=${manifest_status:-missing}, VERSION=${active_version:-missing}, manifest version=${manifest_version:-missing}, manifest SHA=${manifest_sha:-missing}, deployed SHA=${deployed_sha:-missing}"
		return 0
	fi
	print_success "Active runtime bundle metadata is coherent"
	return 0
}
```

title: bug: propagate worktree --issue into ownership registry task ID
body:
## Problem

`worktree-helper.sh add <branch> <path> --issue NNN` parses the explicit issue number and uses it for interactive GitHub claiming, but registers the new worktree without `--task NNN`. The ownership registry therefore stores an empty `task_id`.

This breaks the headless ownership-transfer contract in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: `_hrw_reclaim_stale_worker_worktree_owner()` requires the recorded owner task to equal `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER` before either stale-owner or explicitly allowed clean transfer can proceed. A scheduled same-issue continuation can consequently fail with `worker worktree already has a live owner` even though the caller supplied `--issue` at creation.

Observed while establishing issue #27769 generation 8: the helper created the requested worktree and claimed the issue, but the registry row contained the branch and owner PID with an empty task ID. The row had to be re-registered through the existing registry API before arming continuation.

## Implementation context

- Modify `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` in `cmd_add()` where `explicit_issue` is already parsed and `register_worktree "$path" "$branch"` is called.
- Pass the explicit issue through the existing `register_worktree ... --task <id>` contract in `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry.sh`; preserve empty-task behaviour when `--issue` is omitted.
- Extend the focused worktree-helper tests using existing stubs rather than writing the real global ownership registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- `worktree-helper.sh add ... --issue 123` registers `task_id=123`.
- Creation without `--issue` retains the current empty task ID behaviour.
- Interactive issue claiming remains unchanged.
- Focused tests, ShellCheck, Bash syntax checks, and changed-file linters pass.

## Verification

- Run the focused worktree-helper test covering `cmd_add` registration.
- Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.

Ref #27769

title: Regression: worker DB merge fails when SQLite column order differs
body:
## Description

OpenCode worker session graphs can fail to merge back into the shared database when the worker and shared SQLite tables contain the same named columns in a different physical order. The transaction rolls back and aidevops correctly preserves the worker database, but those sessions remain unavailable through the shared or archive databases.

On aidevops v3.32.147, one observed installation has 81 recovery databases containing 88 distinct sessions; none of those 88 session IDs exist in the shared or archive database. The failure is ongoing on current `main` (`586ce434e8b4`).

This is a regression in the complete worker graph persistence added by PR #27721 for #27687.

## Expected Behavior

Worker session graphs should merge by column name whenever source and destination schemas are compatible, regardless of physical column order. Incompatible schemas should fail with an actionable diagnostic and preserve the recovery database. Existing recovery databases should have an idempotent, verified replay path.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

The following read-only reproducer selects the newest retained recovery DB, creates the current shared `session` schema in memory, then exercises the same positional `SELECT *` assumption without writing to the live database:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3

shared = Path.home() / ".local/share/opencode/opencode.db"
recovery_root = Path.home() / ".aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/worker-db-recovery"
worker = max(
    (path / "opencode.db" for path in recovery_root.iterdir() if (path / "opencode.db").is_file()),
    key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime,
)

def columns(path):
    db = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    result = [row[1] for row in db.execute("PRAGMA table_info(session)")]
    db.close()
    return result

source = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{shared}?mode=ro", uri=True)
create_sql = source.execute(
    "SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='session'"
).fetchone()[0]
source.close()

destination = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
destination.execute(create_sql)
destination.execute("ATTACH DATABASE ? AS worker", (str(worker),))

print("shared_prefix", columns(shared)[:8])
print("worker_prefix", columns(worker)[:8])
try:
    destination.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO main.session SELECT * FROM worker.session")
    print("unexpected success")
except sqlite3.Error as error:
    print(type(error).__name__ + ":", error)
PY
```

**Actual output**:

```text
shared_prefix ['id', 'project_id', 'parent_id', 'slug', 'directory', 'title', 'version', 'share_url']
worker_prefix ['id', 'project_id', 'workspace_id', 'parent_id', 'slug', 'directory', 'path', 'title']
IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: session.slug
```

An inventory check on the same installation reports:

```text
recovery_databases 81
recovery_sessions 88
already_in_shared_or_archive 0
not_visible_in_shared_or_archive 88
```

**Expected output**:

Compatible named columns should be mapped explicitly, and the session graph should merge successfully.

## Root Cause

Commit `c1fdbacf4` added complete graph persistence but retained positional SQLite copies:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1259-1276` checks only which tables expose ownership columns and whether event tables exist; it does not compare each table's named columns or order.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1329-1356` builds `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO main.<table> SELECT * FROM worker.<table>` statements for projects, sessions, session-owned tables, and event tables.
- OpenCode can produce a worker schema with the same `session` columns in a different physical order. SQLite maps `SELECT *` positionally, so values land in the wrong destination columns and the transaction fails on constraints such as `session.slug NOT NULL`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1343` suppresses SQLite stderr, so the lifecycle log records only `db_merge_failed` rather than the failing table and SQLite error.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh:1663-1672` creates source and destination from the same test-schema function, so the regression test cannot expose column-order drift.

The same positional-copy assumption also appears in worker session seeding and should be included in the call-site review.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a headless OpenCode worker whose isolated DB has the current OpenCode column ordering while the shared DB retains an older physical ordering.
2. Allow the worker to exit and `_merge_worker_db` to run.
3. Observe `db_merge_failed` followed by `db_merge_recovery_saved`.
4. Confirm that the worker session exists only in the retained recovery DB.

## Scope and Suggested Verification

- Generate explicit, quoted source/destination column lists from `PRAGMA table_info` rather than using `SELECT *`.
- Define compatibility by named columns and required/default semantics, not physical order.
- Preserve atomic graph replacement and auth-free recovery behavior.
- Surface the failing table and SQLite error without logging session content.
- Add fixtures with identical columns in different orders, missing required columns, and additive compatible columns.
- Add an idempotent recovery replay path that deletes an artifact only after session IDs and child-row counts are verified in the shared DB.
- Verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`, ShellCheck, and the changed-file lint gate.

## Workarounds Applied

- Recovery databases were intentionally left untouched to avoid losing session history.
- The failure was reproduced in an in-memory destination instead of modifying the live shared DB.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.147
- **Latest version**: 3.32.147
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OpenCode version**: 1.18.3
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21
- **gh CLI**: 2.96.0

## Duplicate / Recent-change Checks

- #27687 and merged PR #27721 are the originating feature; this report is a distinct regression in that implementation.
- Searches for `db_merge_failed`, worker DB column order, and SQLite schema merge found no open issue covering this failure.
- Current `main` still contains the positional copies and reproduces the failure.

## Additional Context

The recovery mechanism is working as a safety net, so the evidence does not indicate permanent deletion. However, retained sessions are not visible to normal OpenCode/aidevops session lookup, and recovery storage continues growing until the merge and replay paths are fixed.

title: Regression: managed TMPDIR accumulates OpenCode native libraries
body:
## Description

Managed OpenCode launches route the process-wide `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` variables into the durable aidevops workspace. OpenCode/Bun native scratch libraries are therefore retained under the user's home directory instead of being handled by the operating system's temporary-file lifecycle.

On aidevops v3.32.147, one installation accumulated 258 hidden `*-00000000.so` files using 1,439,322,112 allocated bytes over five days. All 258 files had the same SHA-256 digest, and the count increased during the investigation.

This is a regression from the managed temporary-workspace change in PR #27407 for #27402.

## Expected Behavior

Aidevops should keep deliberate, agent-readable artifacts in its private workspace without converting third-party process scratch into durable user data. OpenCode native scratch should use the host-provided temporary directory or an isolated per-launch directory with a safe lifecycle.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from hashlib import sha256
from datetime import datetime

root = Path.home() / ".aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp"
files = [
    path for path in root.iterdir()
    if path.is_file() and path.name.startswith(".") and path.name.endswith("-00000000.so")
]
digests = {sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in files}
allocated = sum(path.stat().st_blocks * 512 for path in files)
print("files", len(files))
print("allocated_bytes", allocated)
print("unique_sha256", len(digests))
print("oldest", datetime.fromtimestamp(min(path.stat().st_mtime for path in files)).date())
print("newest", datetime.fromtimestamp(max(path.stat().st_mtime for path in files)).date())
PY
```

**Actual output**:

```text
files 258
allocated_bytes 1439322112
unique_sha256 1
oldest: 2026-07-12
newest: 2026-07-17
```

`lsof` showed no process holding the audited files open. Exported symbols identify the library as OpenCode's FFF native component.

**Expected output**:

Repeated managed launches should not leave persistent copies of third-party process scratch in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp`.

## Root Cause

Commit `d380763415` introduced `aidevops_init_temp_workspace()` and exports the durable workspace as all process temp variables:

```text
.agents/scripts/shared-temp-workspace.sh:15 export TMPDIR="$temp_root"
.agents/scripts/shared-temp-workspace.sh:16 export TMP="$temp_root"
.agents/scripts/shared-temp-workspace.sh:17 export TEMP="$temp_root"
.agents/scripts/shared-temp-workspace.sh:18 export AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR="$temp_root"
```

The initializer is called by both `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`. This conflates two different lifecycles:

- `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`: framework-owned artifacts intentionally retained long enough for tools or agents to read.
- `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`: generic process scratch whose lifecycle is normally managed by the OS or launching process.

OpenCode/Bun extracts a native FFF library into the generic process temp directory. Because aidevops redirects that directory into durable home storage and has no matching cleanup lifecycle for this filename, each launch can leave another identical file behind. The first observed file timestamp aligns with the introducing commit, and new files continue to appear.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.32.65 or later with managed OpenCode launching enabled.
2. Launch and close OpenCode repeatedly through the managed launcher or headless runtime.
3. Inspect `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp` for hidden `*-00000000.so` files.
4. Observe repeated identical files accumulating outside the OS temp lifecycle.

## Scope and Suggested Verification

- Preserve `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR` for deliberate framework artifacts.
- Preserve the host-provided process temp variables, or use a per-launch scratch directory with explicit cleanup and crash recovery.
- Do not broadly delete unknown files from the managed workspace.
- Provide a conservative migration for attributable stale native libraries only when no relevant process holds them.
- Update `.agents/scripts/tests/test-managed-temp-workspace.sh` to verify that initialization does not overwrite existing host temp variables.
- Cover interactive and headless launcher call sites on Linux and macOS.
- Verify with the managed-temp, launcher, headless-runtime, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint suites.

## Workarounds Applied

- No native-library files were deleted during diagnosis; they remain available for maintainer verification.
- No process-temp variables were manually overridden, to preserve the reproducer.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.147
- **Latest version**: 3.32.147
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OpenCode version**: 1.18.3
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21
- **gh CLI**: 2.96.0

## Duplicate / Recent-change Checks

- #27402 and merged PR #27407 introduced the current routing to solve permission prompts; this report concerns a distinct persistent-scratch regression caused by that implementation.
- Searches for managed `TMPDIR`, OpenCode temporary libraries, and native-library accumulation found no open issue covering this behavior.
- Current `main` still exports all four variables to the same durable directory.

## Additional Context

The `.so` manifestation is Linux-specific, but the lifecycle boundary is cross-platform: macOS supplies a per-user system `TMPDIR`, and overwriting it can similarly make third-party scratch outlive its intended cleanup policy. The requested outcome is lifecycle separation, not a Linux-only filename cleaner.

title: Enhancement: define bounded storage lifecycles for aidevops-managed data
body:
## Description

Please evaluate a framework-level storage lifecycle for data generated or managed by aidevops. A high-activity installation shows several individually understandable stores growing at the same time—runtime bundles, dependency caches, OpenCode maintenance artifacts, observability, backups, and logs—but there is no consolidated ownership model, bounded default, or safe operator view across them.

This is intentionally an architecture/enhancement request rather than a prescribed implementation. The desired outcome is that routine aidevops use remains storage-bounded and diagnosable without risking active sessions, live runtime leases, rollback safety, worker recovery, or audit history. Maintainers should determine whether this belongs in existing helpers, per-store policies, a reporting surface, upstream coordination, or another design.

Two concrete regressions discovered during the same audit have been separated so this issue does not obscure actionable bugs:

- See-also: #28121 — worker DB merges fail on SQLite column-order drift.
- See-also: #28122 — managed `TMPDIR` retains OpenCode native scratch libraries.

## Problem and Observed Context

Snapshot from one Ubuntu installation running aidevops v3.32.147:

| Store | Observed allocation | Context |
|---|---:|---|
| `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles` | 11.41 GB across 91 bundles | Current policy prunes unleased bundles by age only after 30 days; active, previous, and live-leased bundles are protected. |
| Bundle-local plugin `node_modules` | 6.17 GB across those bundles | Immutable bundles repeat dependency trees; generated npm locks also resolve the omitted OpenCode host peer and platform packages. |
| `~/.local/share/opencode` | 11.75 GB | Includes a 3.92 GB active DB, 3.87 GB WAL, 2.50 GB archive, 803 MB legacy JSON storage, and 287 MB tool output. Some ownership is upstream OpenCode rather than aidevops. |
| Aidevops observability | 2.31 GB | About 1.58 million runtime events plus 302,000 tool-call records; part-stream events and serialized tool metadata dominate growth. |
| Agent backups | 1.31 GB | Ten complete snapshots under the current count policy. |
| Aidevops logs | 454 MB | Includes 2,634 worker failure excerpts plus operational logs without a common byte/age policy. |
| npm cache | 465 MB shortly after cleanup | Runtime bundle dependency installs repopulated it while global tool updates were deferred. |

A prior one-off cleanup of npm cache data and 161 OS-Trash directories reclaimed 37.54 GB, but cleanup alone does not address recurrence. The system currently has adequate free space; this report concerns lifecycle behavior and maintainability, not an emergency disk-pressure claim.

The aggregate pattern appears to be the opportunity: each subsystem makes a local retention or safety decision, but no layer answers how much aidevops-managed storage is expected, what is currently protected, what is safely reclaimable, or whether growth is abnormal.

## Expected Behavior

- Framework-generated storage should have explicit ownership and a bounded or intentionally documented lifecycle.
- Safety-critical artifacts—current/previous bundles, live leases, active DB state, recovery DBs, and required audit records—must remain protected.
- Users should be able to distinguish active data, rollback/recovery data, caches, and safely reclaimable data without inspecting internal directories or SQLite schemas.
- When an update fixes a leak or changes retention, existing attributable leftovers should have a conservative migration or clearly documented cleanup path.
- High growth should be visible before it becomes disk pressure, while normal high-volume use should not produce repeated false alarms.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

After several days of normal interactive/headless work and framework updates:

```bash
du -sh \
  "$HOME/.aidevops/runtime-bundles" \
  "$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability" \
  "$HOME/.aidevops/agents-backups" \
  "$HOME/.aidevops/logs" \
  "$HOME/.local/share/opencode" \
  "$HOME/.npm"
```

**Actual output**:

```text
11.41 GB  runtime bundles (91 bundles)
 2.31 GB  aidevops observability
 1.31 GB  agent backups
 0.45 GB  aidevops logs
11.75 GB  OpenCode data
 0.47 GB  npm cache shortly after cleanup
```

**Expected output**:

The exact size will vary by workload, but unreferenced framework-owned storage should converge under documented policies, and reporting should distinguish protected from safely reclaimable bytes.

**Observation steps**:

1. Run normal interactive and headless aidevops workloads through repeated framework updates and runtime-bundle activations.
2. Observe `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles`, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace`, `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.npm`, and aidevops logs over several days.
3. Note that each area has different or absent retention semantics and that existing cleanup tooling does not present a unified safe/reclaimable view.
4. Clear a cache or old Trash data and observe recurrence from normal framework activity.

## Current Code Context

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:741-789` protects current, previous, and live-leased runtime bundles but otherwise uses a 30-day age threshold without count or byte bounds.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:365-415` installs plugin dependencies separately inside staged bundles.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:655-667` persists every non-`message.updated` OpenCode runtime event.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:848-868` serializes tool metadata without a storage byte limit.
- `.agents/scripts/runtime-events-store.mjs:63-73` enforces append-only runtime events, so retention requires an explicit archival/partitioning design rather than direct deletion.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:767-787` runs active-DB VACUUM during archive passes, while the separate maintenance helper has stronger idle-holder and post-VACUUM checkpoint handling.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:776-800` caps each failure excerpt at 64 KiB but does not impose aggregate age/count/byte retention.
- `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh:26-33` still targets the obsolete `~/.agents` layout rather than the current managed stores.

## Considerations for Maintainers

Please explore the appropriate framework boundary rather than treating the following as required implementation choices:

1. **Ownership:** Which paths are aidevops-owned, jointly managed with OpenCode, or purely third-party/user caches? Aidevops should avoid claiming or deleting data it cannot safely classify.
2. **Safety classes:** Current runtime, previous rollback, live lease, active session, worker recovery, audit history, cache, and disposable scratch need different policies.
3. **Bounds:** Consider whether each framework-owned store needs age, count, byte, or combined soft limits. Limits must never override active references or leases.
4. **Dependency reuse:** Determine whether immutable bundles should continue containing independent dependency trees, use lock-keyed immutable reuse, or rely on more aggressive safe pruning.
5. **OpenCode coordination:** Separate logical session retention from SQLite fragmentation/WAL lifecycle and from upstream-owned legacy/tool-output formats. Avoid deleting data based only on file size.
6. **Observability value:** Preserve terminal, error, lifecycle, and audit evidence while evaluating whether null part-stream telemetry and large raw tool metadata justify their storage cost.
7. **Operator experience:** A read-only status/report may be useful, but this request does not require a new CLI or daemon. Existing update, status, archive, or maintenance paths may be better integration points.
8. **Migration:** Fixes that only stop new growth leave existing bundles, caches, logs, or scratch behind. Any cleanup should be attributable, dry-run capable, and recoverable where practical.
9. **Cross-platform behavior:** Linux and macOS have different temp, Trash, filesystem, and service-management semantics; tests should avoid GNU-only assumptions.
10. **Representativeness:** The measurements come from one high-activity installation. Validate defaults against lower-volume installations before selecting thresholds.

## Non-goals

- Do not automatically delete active OpenCode sessions, worker recovery DBs, current/previous bundles, or live-leased bundles.
- Do not make aidevops responsible for every uv, npm, Playwright, or OS cache merely because it exists on the same machine.
- Do not require speculative custom tooling, content-addressed storage, or a specific `storage doctor` command; those are options for maintainers to assess, not requested acceptance criteria.
- Do not combine the two confirmed regressions above into this architecture task; they have independent reproducers and root causes.

## Suggested Validation Outcomes

- A synthetic update/worker workload demonstrates that unreferenced framework-owned storage converges under the selected policy.
- Current, previous, and live-leased runtime bundles survive every cleanup path.
- Active sessions and retained worker recovery data remain queryable or recoverable.
- Observability retains its defined audit/lifecycle contract while avoiding unintended payload amplification.
- Reporting distinguishes reclaimable bytes from protected bytes and identifies the responsible subsystem.
- Linux and macOS fixture tests cover retention decisions without destructive live-home testing.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually cleared npm cache data and selected stale OS-Trash directories after review, reclaiming 37.54 GB in total.
- Avoided manual deletion of runtime bundles, OpenCode databases, observability data, backups, and worker recovery artifacts because their active/recovery semantics require framework-aware handling.
- Collected measurements and causal evidence per subsystem rather than applying a broad filesystem cleaner.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.147

title: Fail closed before routing review feedback from interactive PRs
body:
## Task

Make Pulse fail closed before routing review feedback from an active `origin:interactive` pull request. Review remediation must select the exact closing issue and must never close the PR or mutate an issue unless worker ownership or a completed stale-interactive handover is proven from current metadata.

## Why

Observed in a managed downstream repository on 2026-07-17:

- A pull request had been created recently, its head had been updated about one minute earlier, and it carried `origin:interactive`.
- Its intended issue was open, assigned to the interactive maintainer, and labeled `status:in-review` plus `origin:interactive`.
- The PR title used `GH#A: ...` and its body used `Resolves #A`; its changed files also included planning context for a separate issue B.
- Pulse logged that `_dispatch_pr_fix_worker` routed the PR's review feedback to issue B. It closed the active PR, appended feedback to issue B, changed B to worker/available ownership, and removed the maintainer assignment.
- No intentional interactive handover had occurred. Manual repair was required to reopen the PR and restore issue B.

This is a destructive provenance failure: uncertain labels, staleness, or linked-issue identity must result in no write.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
  - Harden `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` so an empty caller-supplied label string is authoritatively refreshed instead of being treated as known metadata.
  - Harden `_extract_linked_issue` so a title issue is accepted only when the body contains a closing clause for that same issue. If title/body closing identities disagree or metadata cannot be fetched, log the ambiguity and return no target.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
  - Make `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` require explicit current worker provenance for destructive review routing.
  - Preserve `origin:interactive` PRs unless `_interactive_pr_is_stale` succeeds and handover is confirmed by current `origin:worker-takeover` metadata before dispatch.
  - Fail closed when PR labels, linked-issue metadata, or handover confirmation are unavailable.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh` only if needed to make `_interactive_pr_trigger_handover` return a verifiable applied/already-applied result instead of unconditional success.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh`
  - Replace the historical mismatched-title preference fixture with exact closing-issue matching and ambiguity rejection fixtures.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh`
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh` if the end-to-end review-gate fixture belongs there.

### Reference pattern

Keep the existing mock-`gh` shell-test pattern. Add a regression fixture with:

```text
PR labels: origin:interactive
PR age/head age: fresh
PR title: GH#A: description
PR body: Resolves #A, plus unrelated planning references for B
Issue A: open, origin:interactive, status:in-review, assigned
Review decision: CHANGES_REQUESTED
```

Assert that no `gh pr close`, issue-body edit, origin/status transition, or assignee removal occurs. Add separate mismatch and metadata-read-failure fixtures. Retain a positive worker-origin fixture proving the existing remediation path still routes.

### Complexity impact

Measure `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate`, `_extract_linked_issue`, `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`, and `_interactive_pr_trigger_handover` before editing. Extract focused provenance/identity helpers rather than taking any function above the repository's 100-line shell complexity limit.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh `origin:interactive` PR with an active `status:in-review` issue is never closed or routed by the CHANGES_REQUESTED path.
- An interactive PR is not dispatched unless a stale check passes and `origin:worker-takeover` is confirmed after handover.
- Empty/failed PR-label or issue-metadata reads fail closed with an actionable log line and zero GitHub writes.
- Linked-issue extraction returns only an issue named by a GitHub-native closing clause; title/body mismatch or ambiguous identity returns no target.
- Unrelated issue references or changed planning files cannot influence the routed issue.
- Existing explicit `origin:worker` review-remediation behavior remains covered and passing.
- Regression tests prove no PR-close, issue-body, label, status, or assignee mutation in protected cases.
- Targeted tests pass and ShellCheck reports zero violations.

## Context

- Do not use downstream repository names, issue numbers, PR numbers, or local paths in public comments or fixtures.
- This task is suitable for auto-dispatch once the issue is created; no credentials or external service access are required.
- Prefer redundant fail-closed checks at both target resolution and destructive dispatch boundaries.
