title: Prevent pulse TODO-sync temp workspaces from exhausting disk space
body:
## Description

A shared Linux aidevops host accumulated large per-run TODO-sync clone workspaces under `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse-todo-sync.*`. The cleanup path exists, but it is too conservative for runaway accumulation and can move large workspaces to Trash on the same filesystem instead of reclaiming space.

Observed impact during an operator cleanup session:

- `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp` reached about 107 GiB for one user.
- 318 `pulse-todo-sync.*` workspaces were present; each large workspace was roughly 324-442 MiB.
- `df -hT` improved from `/home` about 353G used / 118G free / 75% to about 133G used / 339G free / 29% after cleanup.
- `/` improved from about 48G used / 47G free / 51% to about 29G used / 66G free / 31% after old `/tmp` cleanup.
- Post-cleanup verification: `remaining_pulse_todo_sync=0`.

This is a framework hygiene bug because routine pulse/TODO-sync operations can create enough stale clone workspaces to repeatedly exhaust disk space on multi-user hosts.

## Expected Behavior

- Stale `pulse-todo-sync.*` workspaces should be reclaimed fast enough to prevent disk pressure.
- Large temporary clone cleanup should free space by default when safe, not move bulk data into Trash on the same filesystem without a retention/prune strategy.
- Framework temp cleanup should cover both `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp` and known `/tmp` pulse/opencode/browser scratch patterns.
- Cleanup should remain safe around active processes and ownership markers.

## Evidence / Relevant Code

Primary files to inspect:

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:52` resolves the TODO-sync temp root to `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:301` moves stale workspaces to `${AIDEVOPS_TODO_SYNC_TRASH_ROOT:-${AIDEVOPS_ORPHAN_TRASH_ROOT:-$HOME/.Trash}}`. On the same filesystem this may not reduce disk usage.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:495` implements `_ptsw_sweep_stale_workspaces`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:499` defaults `PULSE_TODO_SYNC_MAX_RECOVERIES_PER_RUN` to 5, too low for hundreds of stale workspaces.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:524` iterates `pulse-todo-sync.*` candidates.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-temp-helper.sh:57` only cleans pulse worker log files, not clone workspaces or broader temp artifacts.
- `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh:29` targets legacy `$HOME/.agents/tmp`, not `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp`.
- `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh:219` cleans only that legacy tmp directory.

## Workarounds Applied

Manual operator cleanup was required:

- Verified no active process references to `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse-todo-sync.*`.
- Removed all stale `pulse-todo-sync.*` workspaces across user homes.
- Cleared user Trash, npm/npx caches, pnpm stores, Playwright caches.
- Removed old `/tmp` pulse/browser/opencode/temp artifacts not referenced by active processes.

These workarounds recovered about 220 GiB on `/home` and about 19 GiB on `/`.

## Proposed Fix

Implement a bounded, safe, recurring cleanup strategy:

1. Increase or dynamically scale `PULSE_TODO_SYNC_MAX_RECOVERIES_PER_RUN` when stale workspace count or total size exceeds a threshold.
2. Add a direct-delete mode for stale TODO-sync workspaces after ownership/process checks, or make Trash retention size-aware and prune immediately when on the same filesystem.
3. Add a framework cleanup helper that scans `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp` for known owned temp patterns, with dry-run and force modes.
4. Extend scheduled cleanup to run that helper for each aidevops user on shared hosts.
5. Add disk-pressure guardrails: emit warnings or trigger cleanup when temp workspace usage exceeds a configurable size threshold.
6. Add tests covering:
   - many stale `pulse-todo-sync.*` workspaces are cleaned in one or bounded repeated runs;
   - active owner/process workspaces are preserved;
   - markerless legacy workspaces follow the intended retention path;
   - same-filesystem Trash does not count as reclaimed space unless pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A host with hundreds of stale `pulse-todo-sync.*` directories can be reclaimed without manual Python/rm cleanup.
- Cleanup preserves active workspaces and malformed/symlink-unsafe candidates.
- Cleanup behavior is documented/configurable for Trash vs direct removal.
- `system-cleanup.sh` or an equivalent scheduled helper covers `$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp`.
- Tests prove the cleanup no longer caps effective recovery at 5 large stale workspaces when disk pressure exists.

## Verification

Suggested commands:

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-todo-sync-parallel.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-config-helper-tmp-home.sh
```

Add/adjust targeted tests for the new cleanup behavior if existing tests do not cover the disk-pressure case.

## Dispatch Readiness

- Scope: framework bugfix / operational hygiene.
- Suggested tier: standard.
- No secrets required.
- No external services required beyond local tests.
- Worker should avoid including local private paths/usernames in public PR text; use `$HOME` placeholders.

title: Stop repository-metrics startup failures and gate dormant-repository automation
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-29
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive
- **Created by:** AI DevOps for a maintainer-requested live incident
- **Parent task:** #27768 (GitHub API efficiency programme)
- **Conversation context:** A maintainer reported a burst of GitHub mobile notifications saying that the managed repository-metrics workflow failed at startup across many registered repositories, and requested both a systemic fix and a way to keep dormant repositories registered without paying recurring automation/API costs.

## What

Stop the repository-metrics caller from producing zero-job `startup_failure` runs on downstream repositories whose default Actions token permission is read-only. Add a structural regression gate so every canonical reusable-workflow caller grants the exact permission ceiling required by its reusable jobs.

Also introduce an explicit maintained/dormant registration boundary. Repositories remain in `repos.json` for path resolution, history, privacy checks, and deliberate one-repository commands, while recurring Pulse/API scans and cross-repository workflow/badge maintenance omit entries explicitly marked dormant. Existing entries without the new field retain current behaviour.

## Why

Two representative downstream runs reported `conclusion: startup_failure` with zero jobs. Both repositories report `default_workflow_permissions: read`; `.agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml` grants no top-level permissions while `.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml` requests `contents: write`. GitHub therefore rejects the reusable call before creating a job. Every unrelated rollout push retriggers the broken caller, turning one shared template defect into a notification storm.

The local registry currently contains 60 entries: 52 remote repositories, 17 Pulse-enabled repositories, and 35 remote Pulse-disabled repositories. Pulse mostly honours `pulse`, but workflow and badge audits iterate all registrations. Registration, active task automation, and recurring maintenance therefore need separate semantics.

## Reproducer

Using any affected managed downstream repository, the failure is reproducible without executing untrusted code:

```bash
gh run list --repo OWNER/REPOSITORY --workflow "LOC Badge — generate lines-of-code SVGs" \
  --limit 1 --json databaseId,conclusion,status,workflowName
gh api repos/OWNER/REPOSITORY/actions/runs/RUN_ID/jobs \
  --jq '{total_count, jobs: [.jobs[] | {name, conclusion}]}'
gh api repos/OWNER/REPOSITORY/actions/permissions/workflow \
  --jq .default_workflow_permissions
```

Observed on two representative repositories:

```text
conclusion: startup_failure
status: completed
total_count: 0
default_workflow_permissions: read
```

Static contract comparison then shows the rejected elevation:

```text
caller top-level permissions: omitted (inherits contents: read)
reusable job permissions: contents: write
```

The workflow has failed this way since installation, including both weekly schedules and unrelated default-branch pushes. This is confirmed root-cause evidence, not a speculative notification-only report.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** This spans reusable-workflow validation, shell/Python registry selectors, backward-compatible configuration semantics, and cross-repository rollout behaviour. The implementation must distinguish recurring fan-out from explicit one-repository repair and from safety/registry-integrity scans.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The primary interactive session will implement and verify the fix directly after filing this issue.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Memory recall returned no relevant lesson; prework discovery found no open related PR; target files and current downstream failure evidence were verified against current `origin/main` and live GitHub metadata.
- **Verification run:** Representative run metadata, zero-job lists, repository Actions permission defaults, template/reusable workflow contents, and current registry aggregate counts were inspected.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-check current caller/reusable permission unions and registry selectors if another workflow or selector refactor lands before implementation.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml` — add the caller permission ceiling required by the reusable job.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-loc-badge-reusable-install.sh` and/or a reusable caller-contract test — prove the caller/reusable permission union and prevent future templates from escaping validation.
- `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` — document maintained versus dormant registration semantics and backward compatibility.
- `aidevops.sh` and `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` — expose a safe CLI operation/status for changing maintenance state without hand-editing JSON.
- Primary recurring selectors in `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh`, and their focused tests — omit dormant entries in all-repository mode while preserving explicit-repository repair.
- Additional high-cost recurring selectors discovered during implementation where omission would violate the documented maintenance contract; safety cleanup and registry-integrity scans must remain all-repository where required.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** Pulse prefetch/queue consumers, workflow check/sync, badge check/sync, repo list/management commands, monitoring routines that enumerate `initialized_repos`.
- **Writers:** repo registration/update, the new maintenance state command, Pulse expiry migration, and any existing direct JSON migration paths.
- **Tests/fixtures:** reusable workflow caller tests, Pulse registry fixtures, workflow check/sync fixtures, badge selection fixtures, and CLI repo-management fixtures.
- **Schema/docs:** `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`; missing `maintenance` must mean maintained for compatibility.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** framework scripts are deployed by `setup.sh`; downstream caller rollout occurs only after the canonical template fix is merged and verified.
- **Rollback:** removing `maintenance:false` (or setting it true through the CLI) restores prior recurring behaviour; rolling back the permission block would reproduce the zero-job startup failure and is prohibited by the structural test.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `permissions: contents: write` to the repository-metrics caller and validate it equals the union of reusable job permissions.
2. Generalise caller-contract testing so future `*-caller.yml`/`*-reusable.yml` pairs cannot omit or under-grant permission ceilings.
3. Define `maintenance` as an opt-out boolean: missing/true is maintained, false is dormant. `maintenance:false` is ineligible for Pulse even if a stale `pulse:true` remains.
4. Add a repo-management command that changes the field atomically and reports the resulting Pulse/maintenance state; pausing must not delete registration metadata.
5. Apply the predicate to recurring high-cost all-repository paths. Explicit `--repo` operations may inspect/repair a dormant repo, but never override `local_only`, contributor, or authority safety gates.
6. Keep safety cleanup, dirty-state recovery, and registry-integrity operations able to see dormant registrations where omission could leak resources or hide corruption.
7. After merge, roll the corrected caller out with the managed workflow sync path, canary one affected repository, verify a real job starts, then continue a bounded rollout only to maintained repositories.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Existing registries have no `maintenance` field; defaulting missing to false would silently disable all automation. Missing must be treated as true.
- `pulse`, `local_only`, `role`, and `contributed` remain independent task, remote, and authority boundaries; maintenance cannot weaken them.
- Repeated jq selectors and the Python queue scanner can drift. Tests must cover both missing-field inclusion and explicit-false exclusion.
- Explicit one-repository repair should remain possible for dormant repositories so operators can recover them without editing config first.
- Workflow rollout itself creates pushes that retrigger repository metrics; canary verification is required before broad rollout to avoid another notification storm.
- Do not include private repository names or local private paths in public issue, PR, or rollout evidence.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-loc-badge-reusable-install.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh
shellcheck aidevops.sh .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh \
  .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh \
  .agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh
actionlint .github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml \
  .agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml
```

Add focused CLI and registry-selection tests for maintained, dormant, missing-field, explicit-repo, local-only, and contributor cases. Run the repository's relevant changed-file lint gate. For the live canary, require a non-`startup_failure` run with at least one created job before any broader rollout.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A caller generated from the canonical repository-metrics template starts at least one job on a repository with `default_workflow_permissions: read`; it no longer ends as zero-job `startup_failure`.
2. A structural test compares each canonical caller permission map with its reusable workflow's effective job-permission union and fails on an omitted or insufficient permission.
3. Missing/true maintenance state preserves existing recurring behaviour; `maintenance:false` keeps the repo registered but excludes it from recurring Pulse, workflow, and badge fan-out.
4. An explicit one-repository check/repair can target a dormant repo without weakening local-only, contributor, or live permission gates.
5. The CLI updates maintenance state atomically, validates the JSON, and reports how Pulse eligibility changes.
6. The corrected caller is canary-verified live before a bounded maintained-repository rollout; private repository identities are absent from public artifacts.

title: Fix cross-repository full-loop merge evidence resolution
body:
## Problem

Cross-repository use of `full-loop-helper.sh merge` fails closed even after the
target PR has a verified exact head, terminal required checks, and a passing
review-bot result.

Observed during the GH#28844 fleet rollout:

- 32 private repositories reached
  `_required_contexts_for_default_branch`, where the classic branch-protection
  endpoint returned exit 1 instead of a recognized 404. Independent
  `gh pr checks --required` evidence reported no required checks, but the
  full-loop readiness gate remained indeterminate.
- Nine public repositories passed required-check and review-bot gates, then
  `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` failed to materialize pinned commits because
  it inherited the initiating worktree's `origin` rather than resolving the
  explicit target repository passed to `full-loop-helper.sh merge`.

No unsafe retry was used. The rollout required an audited lower-level merge
path with independent exact-head, required-check, review-bot, same-repository,
scope, and review-state validation.

## Reproducer

Use two maintained test repositories, A and B:

1. Enter a linked worktree for A.
2. Open a same-repository PR in B with a terminal exact head and passing review
   evidence.
3. Run `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/B> --squash` from A.
4. For the prospective-tree case, observe that required/review gates pass and
   merge then stops at `unable to materialize pinned PR commits` because A's
   `origin` cannot supply B's commits.
5. For the required-context case, stub the classic branch-protection endpoint
   with GitHub's private-plan unavailable response and return no active
   required-status rulesets. Observe `required-check evidence is indeterminate`
   even though `gh pr checks --required` reports no required checks.

Expected: both paths resolve evidence for B and proceed to the normal merge
policy decision without weakening any indeterminate-error guard.

## Goal

Make explicit-repository full-loop merges independent of the caller's current
Git repository while preserving fail-closed evidence:

1. Resolve prospective merge objects from the target repository identified by
   the merge command, never an unrelated current-worktree remote.
2. Classify the known GitHub response for unavailable classic branch
   protection as empty classic contexts only after active rulesets are queried
   successfully and found not to require checks.
3. Continue failing closed for authentication, rate-limit, malformed-response,
   target mismatch, and ruleset lookup failures.
4. Preserve exact-head binding, human-review guards, prospective TODO checks,
   and audit logging.

## Files to Inspect

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- Existing full-loop merge and required-check tests under
  `.agents/scripts/tests/`

Reference patterns:

- `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` already binds the explicit repository and PR.
- `_required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached` already handles classic
  404 plus rulesets; extend that decision without treating arbitrary exit 1 as
  success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A merge for repository B can run while cwd belongs to repository A and still
  build the prospective tree from B's pinned base/head.
- A fixture for the private-plan classic-protection response plus no active
  required rulesets resolves to no configured required checks.
- Auth/rate/parse and ruleset errors remain indeterminate and block.
- Existing external-author, exact-head, review, and TODO safety tests remain
  green.

## Verification

Add focused regression tests for both failure families, then run the relevant
full-loop merge, required-check resolver, ShellCheck, and local lint suites.

title: Resolve matching non-origin remotes during canonical recovery
body:
## Problem

`canonical-recovery-helper.sh` assumes the canonical GitHub remote is named
`origin`. A maintained repository with a different matching remote can be
rolled out successfully by `sync-workflows-helper.sh` after PR #28850, but the
post-merge canonical synchronization still fails with:

`origin default or configured canonical branch cannot be resolved`

The remote default branch was independently verified current; the local mirror
remained intentionally untouched because recovery failed closed.

## Reproducer

1. Create a canonical test checkout registered as `owner/repository`.
2. Remove `origin` and add the same GitHub repository as remote `github`, with
   fetch and push URLs that both resolve to `owner/repository`.
3. Ensure `github/HEAD` identifies the default branch and the checkout is safe
   for canonical recovery.
4. Run:

   `canonical-recovery-helper.sh fast-forward-current --repo <checkout> --branch main --issue <N> --confirm FAST_FORWARD_CANONICAL_BRANCH`

Observed: recovery stops with `origin default or configured canonical branch
cannot be resolved`. Expected: it validates and uses `github` without changing
remote configuration.

## Goal

Resolve the Git remote whose fetch and push identities match the registered
GitHub repository, and use it consistently throughout canonical recovery.

Requirements:

- Support common HTTPS, SSH, and git GitHub URL forms and case-insensitive
  owner/repository matching.
- Prefer exact fetch-plus-push identity matches.
- Do not mutate remote configuration or assume `origin` when another GitHub
  identity is present.
- Retain a narrowly documented `origin` fallback only for mirrors where no
  configured remote is parseable as GitHub, if that remains compatible with
  canonical-recovery trust guarantees.
- Fail closed for mismatched or ambiguous GitHub remotes.

## Files to Inspect

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` remote-resolution implementation
  from PR #28850 as the reference pattern

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fast-forward-current` and `sync-mirror` work in a canonical checkout whose
  matching remote is named `github` and where no `origin` exists.
- A non-matching `origin` plus a matching alternate remote selects only the
  matching remote.
- Fetch, default-branch resolution, pinned remote refs, compare-and-swap, and
  final verification all use the selected remote.
- Mismatched/ambiguous remote tests fail before canonical mutation.

## Verification

Add isolated remote fixtures covering renamed, mismatched, and ambiguous
remotes; run canonical recovery tests, ShellCheck, and local lint.

title: Honor check-workflows help without running inventory
body:
## Problem

Running `./aidevops.sh check-workflows --help` executed the full workflow
inventory instead of printing command help. The command enumerated registered
repository identifiers and continued until the tool timeout.

A help request must be side-effect-free, bounded, and must not read or print the
repository registry.

## Reproducer

1. Initialize aidevops with at least one repository registry entry.
2. From an aidevops linked worktree, run
   `./aidevops.sh check-workflows --help`.
3. Observe that classification rows begin printing instead of bounded usage
   text; with a larger registry the command continues until timeout.

Expected: usage only, exit 0, and no registry access. Repeat with `-h`.

## Goal

Forward `-h` and `--help` correctly through the top-level `check-workflows`
command route so the helper prints usage and exits immediately.

## Files to Inspect

- `aidevops.sh`
- The CLI command-routing module used by `check-workflows`
- `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh`
- Existing CLI dispatch tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`

The helper already implements `-h|--help`; preserve that implementation rather
than duplicating help text in the top-level CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `./aidevops.sh check-workflows --help` prints only bounded usage text and
  exits 0.
- `./aidevops.sh check-workflows -h` behaves identically.
- Neither command reads `repos.json`, starts classification, contacts GitHub,
  nor emits repository identifiers.
- Normal `check-workflows` flags continue to pass through unchanged.

## Verification

Add a CLI routing regression test with a registry sentinel that fails if read,
then run the targeted CLI tests and local lint.

title: Integrate parallel knowledge providers into the shared registry
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `knowledge provider registry integration DEV Forem HubSpot Discourse` returned no reusable lesson.
- [x] Discovery pass: eleven distinct provider leaves were verified with disjoint provider-specific files and one shared integration boundary; DEV Community maps to new Forem child #29034, while HubSpot Community maps to the already merged generic Discourse provider #28673.
- [x] File refs verified: helper, sync, import, store, capability matrix, aggregate tests, and current provider-specific patterns exist on current `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` because eleven heterogeneous live/archive/manual/no-route contracts must converge without ordering dependence, schema drift, or outbound mutation reachability.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped because integration must inspect the actual merged provider contracts rather than predicted interfaces.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-29; expanded 2026-07-30 and 2026-07-31.
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive sessions.
- **Parent task:** #28659.
- **Blocked by:** #28782, #28783, #28784, #28785, #28786, #28787, #28952, #28953, #28954, #28955, and #29034 through GitHub native relationships.
- **Blocks:** #28788 through a GitHub native relationship.
- **Conversation context:** Provider workers own disjoint implementation, fixture, and content files so they can run concurrently. This task owns shared registry wiring, aggregate compatibility, and the evidence-backed capability matrix after all eleven outcomes merge.

## What

Integrate the independently implemented Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Signal, Nextcloud Talk, Gumroad, Google Business Profile, Telegram, Binance Square, Bluesky, and Forem contracts into the provider-neutral knowledge registry. Support each merged live, archive, hybrid, manual, or no-route outcome without provider-name conditionals leaking into unrelated paths.

Forem child #29034 targets DEV Community first but must retain multi-instance identity. HubSpot Community requires no new provider contract because its rendered platform is Discourse and merged child #28673 already supplies multi-instance Discourse collection.

## Why

Letting each provider edit shared registration, store adapters, aggregate tests, or the matrix would serialize and conflict otherwise parallel work. A dedicated integration gate can evaluate the final contracts together, reject ambiguous identities, preserve canonical #28779 storage, and prove no collector reaches messaging, listing, commerce, financial, publishing, moderation, or other mutation surfaces.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Eleven independently designed provider outcomes coordinate more than four shared files and require architecture, compatibility, security, migration, and aggregate-test judgment.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped.
- **Rationale:** A seed before provider merges would anchor integration to interfaces that may legitimately resolve as live, export-only, manual, or no-route.
- **Status:** `not-created`.
- **Freshness evidence:** The native dependency graph, current shared files, Forem child #29034, and HubSpot-to-Discourse deduplication were verified on 2026-07-31.
- **Verification run:** `UNVERIFIED — integration has not started`.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-read every merged provider contract/test and the current shared registry before changing shared files.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** the eleven merged provider public contracts and focused tests to extract exact provider IDs, aliases, modes, command boundaries, receipts, coverage, and no-write guarantees.
- **Then read:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge-social-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_sync.py`, `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_import.py`, `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_store.py`, and aggregate tests only for the shared adapters those contracts require.
- **Load only if:** a provider exposes an incompatible contract; inspect its merged PR and file a provider-specific regression instead of silently repairing it here.
- **Stop when:** registration order, aliases, live/import/manual/no-route dispatch, persistence compatibility, matrix evidence, and aggregate no-write behavior are deterministic.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/knowledge-social-helper.sh` — deterministic provider registration and provider-neutral command dispatch.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/knowledge_social_sync.py` — only where merged contracts require a provider-neutral live-sync adapter.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/knowledge_social_import.py` — only where merged contracts require a provider-neutral archive/import adapter.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/knowledge_social_store.py` — only if merged contracts expose a provider-neutral persistence gap; preserve #28779 canonical identity.
- `EDIT: .agents/aidevops/knowledge-plane/06-social-provider-capabilities.md` — update solely from merged implementation/test evidence, including a Forem row and no duplicate HubSpot row.
- `EDIT: .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh` — aggregate registration, routing, no-write, and order-independence regressions.
- `EDIT: .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social.sh` — aggregate store/query/backward-compatibility regressions.

Do not edit provider-specific implementation, fixture, content, or communications-reference files. Report a defective merged provider contract against its provider issue/PR.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge-social-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_sync.py`, and `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_import.py` read provider IDs, aliases, modes, commands, connection policy, and receipts.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_sync.py`, `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_import.py`, and `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_store.py` write provider-neutral evidence/checkpoints only; the capability matrix is the sole documentation writer.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh`, `.agents/tests/test-knowledge-social.sh`, and all eleven provider-focused tests encode the contracts being integrated.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_store.py` and `.agents/aidevops/knowledge-plane/06-social-provider-capabilities.md` define shared persistence/capability shape; schema changes require evidence from at least one merged provider gap.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Shared helper/modules/docs deploy through `setup.sh`; no provider credentials, private IDs, exports, paths, content, or runtime corpus data enter git.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge_social_store.py` owns any additive compatibility migration proven necessary; existing provider evidence/checkpoints remain readable and no migration is added speculatively.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/knowledge-social-helper.sh`, sync/import adapters, and store migration logic must allow provider registration rollback without deleting provider-specific raw evidence, receipts, or checkpoints.

### Implementation Steps

1. Inspect each merged provider contract, help surface, focused fixtures, and terminal receipts; record exact provider identity, aliases, live/import/manual/no-route modes, and shared adapter needs.
2. Register all eleven provider identities without ordering dependence, duplicate aliases, ambiguous command routing, or fallback to another provider. Register Forem once; do not register DEV and Forem as separate providers.
3. Connect shared sync/import/store paths only where merged contracts prove a generic adapter is needed. Prefer capability interfaces over provider-name branches.
4. Preserve strict no-write separation from existing outbound bot, social, listing, commerce, publishing, moderation, account, trading, wallet, and payment routes; reject credentials or contracts that broaden authority.
5. Update the capability matrix solely from merged implementation and fixture evidence, retaining unsupported, approval, permission, retention, export, manual, private, and no-safe-route gaps. Keep HubSpot under the existing Discourse row rather than adding a duplicate provider.
6. Add aggregate tests loading providers in different orders, rejecting duplicate IDs/aliases, exercising every merged mode, and proving existing providers remain unchanged.
7. Treat Bluesky as the existing implementation for the #28675 candidate row and Forem as the generic family for DEV Community so later provider research deduplicates rather than filing site-specific children.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Integration runs only after all native blockers close; registration construction must be deterministic and duplicate detection must fail before mutating runtime state.
- **Migration/rollback:** Additive shared migration only when merged contracts prove it; rollback preserves old readers and all provider-specific evidence/checkpoints.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Existing providers and partially deployed runtimes continue to reject unknown providers safely; no provider becomes a default fallback.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated registration and sync/import dispatch select the same provider/mode and cannot duplicate aliases, migrations, evidence, or checkpoints.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** One defective provider contract fails its registration/aggregate test without disabling unrelated providers or being patched out of scope.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-slack.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-discord.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-whatsapp.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-signal.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-nextcloud-talk.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-gumroad.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-google-business-profile.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-telegram.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-binance-square.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-bluesky.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-forem.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social-sync.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-knowledge-social.sh
python3 -m compileall -q .agents/scripts
shellcheck .agents/scripts/knowledge-social-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** focused tests prove every input contract; aggregate tests prove registration/order/routing/no-write compatibility; compile, ShellCheck, and changed-file lint cover shared implementation/docs.
- **Broad verification trigger:** shared registry/store changes already justify all provider-focused plus aggregate tests; no unrelated full-repository gate is required unless setup/root tooling changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] All eleven focused provider tests and aggregate social tests pass.
- [ ] WIP commit created before broader gates: `wip: integrate parallel knowledge providers`.
- [ ] Changed-file lint and any evidence-triggered setup verification then run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All eleven provider-specific contracts register and route deterministically regardless of registration order.
- [ ] Duplicate or ambiguous provider identities fail closed without corrupting checkpoints or selecting another provider; DEV maps only to `forem`, while HubSpot Community continues to map only to `discourse`.
- [ ] Shared sync/import/store behavior supports every merged live/archive/hybrid/manual/no-route mode without provider-specific logic leaking into unrelated paths.
- [ ] Aggregate tests prove collector routes cannot invoke outbound message, reaction, upload, moderation, publishing, listing, account, financial, trading, wallet, payment, or commerce mutations.
- [ ] The capability matrix reflects verified merged behavior and explicit gaps; it does not claim untested credentials, plans, approvals, exports, private state, unavailable history, or a duplicate HubSpot provider.
- [ ] Existing providers and all provider-specific tests remain green, no provider-specific file is modified, and #28675 is directed to deduplicate Bluesky and Forem families.

## Context & Decisions

- Provider leaves own only provider-specific files; this task owns all shared registration and capability-matrix changes.
- The integration accepts implemented and evidence-backed no-route outcomes equally; it never creates placeholder routes to make the matrix appear complete.
- Google Business Profile and Binance Square require explicit listing/financial mutation isolation beyond the standard social no-write boundary.
- DEV Community is a Forem instance and is represented by #29034. HubSpot Community is a Discourse instance and is already represented by merged #28673, so it adds no new blocker or provider identity.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** #28782, #28783, #28784, #28785, #28786, #28787, #28952, #28953, #28954, #28955, and #29034.
- **Blocks:** #28788.
- **External:** live provider credentials, paid plans, API approvals, private exports, and operator schedules are optional and never merge gates; fixture-backed behavior fails closed without them.

title: Fix invalid rate-limit selections in native relationship mutations
body:
Goal: restore creation and removal of native GitHub blocked-by and sub-issue relationships through the canonical issue-sync helper. Observed evidence: on v3.32.195, invoking `_gh_add_sub_issue` with two valid issue node IDs returned GraphQL `undefinedField` at `mutation.rateLimit` with `Field rateLimit does not exist on type Mutation`; the same impossible selection appears in `_gh_add_blocked_by` and `_gh_remove_blocked_by`. title: t18182: fix(simplification-state): preserve a clean canonical checkout across refresh publication
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# t18182: Preserve a clean canonical checkout across simplification-state refresh publication

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `simplification-state publication canonical dirty` → 0 hits — no prior reusable lesson was available before discovery
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 recent source commit / 1 relevant merged PR / 0 open PRs — PR #28228 introduced checkout-free publication, while commit `88e4b8feb` later added receipt/handoff security that this fix must preserve
- [x] File refs verified: 12 refs checked against current `origin/main`, all present
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — five coordinated shell/test surfaces, a shared publication security boundary, and more than 2,000 source lines to synthesize
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — issue-only avoids anchoring the worker to an untested external-snapshot API

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-07-29
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive diagnosis and auto-dispatch handoff
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive), directed by the maintainer
- **Parent task:** None; leaf regression task for GH#28872
- **Blocked by:** None
- **Conversation context:** Post-rollout cleanup found the canonical checkout dirty only because simplification maintenance had refreshed the tracked registry before publishing it checkout-free. The user requested a worker-ready auto-dispatch fix rather than folding generated state into unrelated PRs.

## What

Make the complete simplification-state refresh, same-cycle scan, and publication lifecycle operate on an isolated state snapshot. A successful, no-op, conflicting, or failed publication must leave the canonical checkout's HEAD, index, tracked files, and untracked files unchanged while retaining the existing allowlist, lease, publication-ID, handoff receipt, and retry guarantees.

## Why

PR #28228 / issue #28225 replaced canonical `git add`/commit/push with checkout-free `commit-tree` publication, but it covered only the publisher's own before/after behavior. The caller still mutates `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json` first. On 2026-07-29 the canonical checkout showed that file modified while one commit behind; its entire local diff exactly matched checkout-free publication commit `f5ac0cecd`. This benign residue blocks clean canonical synchronization and creates false concern during parallel full-loop sessions.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The invariant is decided, but the worker must design a narrowly scoped external-source snapshot contract across a security-sensitive publisher and the weekly scan lifecycle without growing two near-threshold shell orchestrators.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: title the implementation PR `t18182: ...` and use `Resolves #28872`.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Current discovery proves the bug and boundaries, but the safest publisher API should be implemented and tested together by the worker.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Source, callers, tests, PR #28228, commit `88e4b8feb`, and live commit `f5ac0cecd` checked on 2026-07-29.
- **Verification run:** Discovery only; implementation tests are unrun.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-read `planning-publisher.sh` receipt/snapshot helpers if another planning-publication change lands before dispatch.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:276-335,470-557` — locate state refresh, same-cycle state consumers, and orchestration size constraints.
- **Then read:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh:164-352` — preserve branch guards, mutation semantics, and publication result handling.
- **Load only if changing the publisher contract:** `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh:53-109,649-810` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh:285-398` — preserve path allowlisting, blob snapshots, leases, receipts, conflict handling, and replay.
- **Why:** The fix must isolate state generation without weakening a recently hardened checkout-free publication boundary.
- **Stop when:** The worker can name the temporary-state owner, destination/source validation contract, cleanup behavior, and tests for success/no-op/conflict/failure.

### Worker Quick-Start

1. `_simplification_state_refresh`, `_simplification_state_prune`, and `_simplification_state_backfill_closed` already accept an arbitrary `state_file`; use that seam rather than rewriting their mutation logic.
2. `_simplification_state_push` currently hardcodes the repository-relative source at `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh:325-345`; it needs a validated external source while preserving that exact destination.
3. `run_weekly_complexity_scan` passes the canonical state path to refresh and both language scans at `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:530-536`; all three consumers must share one isolated snapshot for the cycle.
4. Existing test `test_simplification_state_scope_preserves_checkout` snapshots an already-dirty fixture before calling only the publisher. Add an end-to-end clean-fixture regression that performs refresh plus publication.
5. Do not restore/reset the canonical file after publication. Prevent every canonical write instead.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:276-335,470-557` — own a temporary state snapshot across refresh, publication, and same-cycle scans without growing the orchestrators inline.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh:164-352` — publish a caller-supplied state snapshot to the fixed registry destination while preserving branch and result semantics.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh:53-109,649-810` — add a narrowly allowlisted destination/source snapshot seam; keep source paths out of durable receipts and trees.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh:285-398` — cover external-source allowlisting, receipt integrity, replay, conflict, and rejection cases.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-publication-isolation.sh` — exercise the refresh-to-publish lifecycle from a clean canonical fixture.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `run_weekly_complexity_scan` calls `_complexity_scan_state_refresh`, then passes the same state file to `_complexity_scan_lang_shell` and `_complexity_scan_lang_md`; `complexity-scan-helper.sh` reads the supplied registry.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_simplification_state_refresh`, `_simplification_state_prune`, and `_simplification_state_backfill_closed` mutate their `state_file`; `_simplification_state_push` delegates to `planning_publish`; `_planning_publish_snapshot` writes blobs and `planning_publish` advances the remote ref with a lease.
- **Tests/fixtures:** Existing publisher coverage is in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh`; state preservation coverage also exists in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-preserve.sh`; add the end-to-end isolation fixture named above.
- **Schemas/config:** Preserve `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json` JSON shape and `aidevops-planning-publication-v2` receipt format. An external source path is runtime-only and must not enter either schema.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys repository scripts; no generated copy is edited directly. The registry remains a tracked generated state file on the remote default branch.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the persisted registry and receipt schemas remain unchanged; existing files stay readable and the next scan uses the same JSON through a temporary copy.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh` owns temporary-snapshot cleanup; rollback reverts the coordinated caller/publisher changes and must never reset, stash, clean, or delete canonical user state.

### Implementation Steps

1. Introduce a focused helper that creates a private temporary copy of the tracked registry and returns/owns its cleanup. Keep temporary artifacts under the framework agent workspace when available, with `mktemp` fallback consistent with existing shell helpers.
2. Pass that one snapshot through prune, refresh, recently-closed backfill, publication, and both same-cycle language scans. If no state changes, skip publication but still scan against and clean the snapshot.
3. Extend `_simplification_state_push` and the publisher through a narrow destination/source contract: destination remains exactly `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`; source must be a regular, non-symlink file; generic planning publication behavior stays unchanged.
4. Bind publication IDs and receipts to the destination path plus blob, never to the local temporary pathname. Preserve force-with-lease contention, retryable conflict return `2`, no-op replay, validator behavior, and handoff verification from `88e4b8feb`.
5. Add hermetic tests proving clean-checkout invariance across successful refresh/publication, no-op, injected contention, validation failure, and malformed/symlink external-source rejection. Assert the same-cycle scanner reads the refreshed snapshot.
6. Keep generated registry updates out of the implementation PR; tests create fixtures only.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Multiple pulse instances may derive snapshots from different source HEADs. Existing parent-conflict checks and force-with-lease behavior remain authoritative; a loser returns retryable conflict without touching canonical state or overwriting the winner.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration. Do not add a cleanup step that resets canonical paths, because it could erase a parallel human edit. Reverting the feature restores the old call path without changing stored JSON.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Preserve ordinary `planning_publish` callers and current one-path snapshots. Keep `_simplification_state_push` callable by existing tests or update every in-repo caller atomically within this PR.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Replaying identical destination/blob content must remain a no-op with the same remote commit semantics; temporary filenames must not affect publication IDs or receipts.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Temp creation, JSON mutation, validation, receipt, or push failure must clean temporary files, retain canonical bytes/index/HEAD, and leave the objective retryable on the next pulse.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target functions:** `planning_publish` (currently 98 lines), `run_weekly_complexity_scan` (81 lines), `_complexity_scan_state_refresh` (59 lines), and `_simplification_state_push` (28 lines).
- **Estimated growth:** Approximately +60-120 production lines plus tests.
- **Projected post-change:** `planning_publish` and `run_weekly_complexity_scan` would exceed or crowd the 100-line function gate if logic is added inline.
- **Action required:** Add/extract focused snapshot-source and state-lifecycle helpers first; keep both existing orchestrators at or below their current sizes.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-publication-isolation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-preserve.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-publication-isolation.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** Isolation test proves the end-to-end canonical invariant and same-cycle state use; publisher tests prove source/destination validation, receipts, retries, and conflicts; preserve test protects registry semantics; full-loop test protects the recent publication-receipt merge bridge; ShellCheck and changed lint cover shell quality.
- **Broad verification trigger:** The shared planning publisher is a full-loop merge boundary, so its focused full-loop merge suite is required. No release or full repository gate is required unless the changed-file linter finds broader coupling.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused tests pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-publication-isolation.sh && bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broader gates: `wip: isolate simplification state publication`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broader verification then run: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh && .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Keep canonical checkouts pristine throughout simplification-state refresh and checkout-free publication.
- **Preserved user directions:** Deliver this as a worker-ready auto-dispatch fix; do not create a duplicate worktree-cleanup mechanism.
- **Trigger and evidence:** Not triggered; network/rate-limit or publication conflict may pause only the push path.
- **Completed and verified:** The regression and prior partial fix are documented; implementation remains open.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** All criteria below until code and tests merge.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** Resetting/restoring canonical files after the fact or adding generated state to unrelated feature PRs.
- **Next safe route:** Continue from the isolated snapshot with hermetic publisher fixtures; preserve a WIP commit before broad gates.
- **Resume condition:** Focused isolation and publisher suites pass with canonical before/after digests identical.
- **Owner and status:** Auto-dispatch worker; not-triggered.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-state-publication-isolation.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The refresh-and-publication lifecycle must not alter a clean canonical fixture's HEAD, index, tracked working files, or untracked-file inventory.
- [ ] The remote default branch receives only `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`, and its content equals the refreshed isolated snapshot.
- [ ] Shell and Markdown scans in the same cycle consume the refreshed snapshot rather than stale canonical state.
- [ ] No-op replay, concurrent remote contention, validator failure, and interrupted publication leave canonical state unchanged and retain existing return/retry semantics.
- [ ] External snapshot sources are accepted only for the exact scope/destination contract; symlinks, directories, unauthorized destinations, and malformed sources fail closed before push.
- [ ] Publication IDs, handoff receipts, and idempotence depend on destination/blob content, not nondeterministic temporary paths.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, the full-loop publication bridge suite, and changed-file lint pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Keep generated simplification state in dedicated automated commits; do not add it to unrelated implementation PRs.
- Prevent canonical writes instead of restoring/resetting afterward, because post-hoc cleanup can race with parallel human work.
- Reuse the state functions' existing arbitrary `state_file` parameters and the publisher's index/commit-tree model.
- Treat PR #28228 as a partial fix: it stopped staging/committing in canonical but did not isolate the caller's preceding mutation.
- Preserve the receipt/handoff hardening from commit `88e4b8feb` and the exact publication behavior observed in `f5ac0cecd`.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:276-335` — refresh/prune/backfill and publish coordinator.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:470-557` — weekly scan lifecycle and same-state consumers.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh:164-352` — registry mutation and hardcoded publication source.
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh:53-109` — scope allowlist and source-file snapshot construction.
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh:649-810` — snapshot preparation, candidate build, lease push, receipts, and replay.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh:285-398` — current publisher-only simplification tests whose fixture starts dirty.
- PR #28228 / issue #28225 — prior checkout-free publication change.
- Commit `88e4b8feb` — publication receipt/handoff bridge that must remain intact.
- Commit `f5ac0cecd` — live generated-state commit exactly matching the observed canonical residue.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** None.
- **Blocks:** Reliable clean canonical synchronization and lower-noise parallel full-loop preflight.
- **External:** Existing authenticated GitHub environment for live publication; all regression tests must be hermetic and use local bare remotes.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 45m | Reconfirm publisher receipt and caller contracts |
| Implementation | 1h 45m | Snapshot lifecycle and external-source publication seam |
| Testing | 1h 30m | End-to-end isolation, conflict, receipt, lint, full-loop bridge |

title: Reconcile terminal outcomes before Pulse capacity and launch-pressure accounting
body:
## Description

Pulse capacity, current-state guardrails, and adaptive launch staggering classify raw headless-runtime terminal rows as failures even after durable objective reconciliation marks the same attempts successful. In the live 15-minute window, raw results were `permission_required` (3), `post_pr_handoff` (1), and `success` (1), while `worker-activity-helper.sh` reconciled all 5 attempts to effective success. Pulse consequently reported 4 terminal failures and reduced the configured worker target from 24 to 12.

This is a follow-up regression gap after #28847; #27907 established durable `attempt_outcome` records as the canonical terminal disposition.

## Expected Behavior

Generic terminal success/failure pressure must use the latest matching durable attempt outcome when present. Raw provider signals such as rate limits, provider 5xx responses, and exhausted service interruptions must continue to reduce capacity even when the overall objective later succeeds. Unknown or unmatched legacy rows must retain current raw-result behavior.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

```bash
.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 15m --json
.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 1h --json --no-pr-check
```

**Actual output:**

- `dispatch_capacity_recent_failures=4` and `dispatch_capacity_final_max_workers=12` from a raw target of 24.
- Current-state raw counts: 1 success, 4 failures.
- Worker activity for the same 5 attempt IDs: 5 effective successes, 0 effective failures.
- `objective-evidence.jsonl` contains matching `attempt_outcome` records with `effective_outcome=success` for the four non-success raw results.

## Causal Status

Confirmed. Commit `4967e4465` added worker-role filtering but the three production readers still evaluate raw `result`/`exit_code` fields directly. Production call chain: `pulse-wrapper.sh` sources `pulse-capacity.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`; the engine sources `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh`. Capacity calls `pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap`; dispatch uses `_dispatch_apply_current_state_guardrails` and `_dispatch_inter_launch_delay`.

## Complete Write Surface

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: capacity health counts.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh`: current success/failure guardrail counts.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: adaptive launch-pressure counts.
- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`: reference reconciliation semantics; avoid duplicating a conflicting outcome policy.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: focused capacity/guardrail regression coverage.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-staggering.sh`: launch-delay regression coverage if the shared path is not already exercised.

No schema migration or backfill is required; raw metrics and durable objective evidence remain unchanged.

## Hazards and Compatibility

- Preserve legacy behavior when no exact attempt outcome exists.
- Match by non-empty `attempt_id` and validate repository/issue identity when present.
- Use the latest matching evidence timestamp.
- Do not suppress raw rate-limit, provider-5xx, or exhausted-service-interruption counters after objective success.
- Keep the read bounded to recent metrics and a bounded tail of objective evidence.
- Fail open to existing raw-result accounting when evidence is missing or malformed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A raw `permission_required` or `post_pr_handoff` row with an exact effective-success outcome contributes success and zero generic failures.
- A reconciled failed attempt still contributes one generic failure.
- A raw rate-limit/provider-error signal still contributes its provider-health counter even if the terminal objective later succeeds.
- Unmatched legacy rows preserve the existing success/failure classification.
- Live Pulse no longer halves capacity solely because successful reconciled lifecycle handoffs have non-success raw result tokens.

## Verification

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-staggering.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-staggering.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
```

## Workarounds Applied

None. The configured cap remains 24; no safety gate was bypassed.

title: bug(pr-review-thread-response-scanner): worker prompt hardcodes 'bot finding' — human reviewer praise threads never resolved when INCLUDE_HUMAN=true
body:
## Description

`_prrts_write_prompt_file()` in `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` generates the worker prompt with a hardcoded `"bot finding"` scope label at line 1167, even when dispatched with `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`. Workers correctly identify that the human thread author is not a bot and conclude the instruction does not apply to them — they call `mark-blocked` instead of resolving. After 9 repeated attempts with the same fingerprint, the circuit breaker fires and dispatch stops permanently. The merge-blocking human thread remains unresolved indefinitely.

## Expected Behavior

When dispatched with `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`, the generated prompt should scope the classification instruction to "review thread (bot or human reviewer)" and include a hint that human confirmations/approvals count as praise-only. Workers should then correctly resolve praise-only human threads without code changes.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# pulse-merge.sh:128 — triggered automatically when PR merge hits "A conversation must be resolved"
PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true \
  pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr Majowka/mesh-manager /home/ubuntu/Git/mesh-manager 3208
# Returns exit 1 after 9 prior attempts (logged as "dispatch failed")
```

**Actual output**:

```
# Scanner state file (Majowka-mesh-manager-3208.state):
fingerprint=PRRT_kwDOPhWWNs6UU7RD:https://github.com/Majowka/mesh-manager/pull/3208#discussion_r3663824640
dispatched_at=1785270216
thread_count=1
attempt_count=9
last_head_sha=9f591f6d2f08bc21bbcc4bfadeb48ddab0606605
maintainer_attention=true
attention_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint

# Pulse log (repeated each merge cycle):
[pulse-merge] review-thread remediation dispatch failed for PR #3208 in Majowka/mesh-manager after required unresolved review-thread preflight blocker
```

**Expected output**: Worker resolves the praise-only thread; `mark-complete` is called; PR merges on next cycle.

**Production entry point**: `pulse-merge.sh:128` calls the scanner with `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true` when a merge attempt hits "A conversation must be resolved":

```bash
# pulse-merge.sh:128
if ! PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true "$scanner" dispatch-pr "$repo_slug" "$repo_path" "$pr_number"
```

**Call chain**:
1. `pulse-merge.sh:128` calls `pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr` with `INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`
2. `_prrts_dispatch_guarded()` calls `_prrts_dispatch_worker()` calls `_prrts_write_prompt_file()`
3. `_prrts_write_prompt_file()` writes heredoc with hardcoded `"bot finding"` at line 1167 — **bug here**
4. Worker receives human thread (e.g. `kamcio2603`) + prompt saying "For each unresolved bot finding"
5. Worker: author is not a bot, instruction doesn't apply, calls `mark-blocked` with `decision`
6. `_prrts_should_escalate_attempt()` sees same fingerprint after N attempts, circuit breaker fires, `maintainer_attention=true`
7. Pulse logs `"review-thread remediation dispatch failed"` every cycle; merge permanently blocked

**Symptom** (observed on PR #3208, Majowka/mesh-manager):

```
# Scanner state after 9 failed dispatch attempts:
fingerprint=PRRT_kwDOPhWWNs6UU7RD:...
attempt_count=9
maintainer_attention=true
attention_reason=same_unresolved_thread_fingerprint
```

```
# Pulse log (repeated every cycle):
[pulse-merge] review-thread remediation dispatch failed for PR #3208 in Majowka/mesh-manager after required unresolved review-thread preflight blocker
```

The unresolved thread is a human confirmation: *"Reviewed this critical path: the existing synchronous XLSX renderer is correctly moved off the event loop..."* — a clear praise-only comment that should be resolved immediately.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Causal code**:

```
9b5852067b (Marcus Quinn 2026-07-24 19:39:37 +0100 1167) 4. For each unresolved bot finding, classify it as actionable or praise-only:
```

The line was authored by commit `9b5852067` (PR #28579 — "enforce review worker terminal-state contract"). Bug #6 ("Scanner prompt says 'bot review threads' even with INCLUDE_HUMAN=true") was identified in local commit `2c1cb5d1c` but was not included in PR #24540 which introduced `INCLUDE_HUMAN` support.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-merge.sh:128` — `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true "$scanner" dispatch-pr` called when merge hits "A conversation must be resolved"
- **Call chain**: `pulse-merge.sh:128` calls `_pulse_merge_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` calls scanner `dispatch-pr` calls `_prrts_dispatch_guarded` calls `_prrts_dispatch_worker` calls `_prrts_write_prompt_file` (line 1621) — writes heredoc with `"bot finding"` at line 1167 regardless of `INCLUDE_HUMAN`
- **Integrated verification**: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` exercises the dispatch path. Bug can be confirmed directly: `PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true bash -c 'source .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh; grep "bot finding" "$(PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true _prrts_write_prompt_file slug path 1 title 1 fp preview)"'` — returns a match, proving the prompt is not adapted to `INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`

## Fix

In `_prrts_write_prompt_file()`, declare a local variable before the heredoc (after line 1124), and reference it at line 1167:

```bash
# After line 1124 (prompt_file= assignment), add:
local _thread_kind_desc="bot finding"
local _human_thread_hint=""
if [[ "${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
    _thread_kind_desc="review thread (bot or human reviewer)"
    _human_thread_hint="   - Human reviewer confirmations ('Reviewed this', 'LGTM', 'Verified', 'Looks good') are praise-only even when written by a non-bot account — do not edit code, resolve directly."
fi
```

Then in the heredoc at line 1167:

```diff
-4. For each unresolved bot finding, classify it as actionable or praise-only:
+4. For each unresolved ${_thread_kind_desc}, classify it as actionable or praise-only:
```

And after the praise-only bullet (line 1172), add:

```diff
     resolve with '${scanner_path} resolve ${repo_slug} <thread_id>'.
+   ${_human_thread_hint}
```

## Verification

```bash

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh

# 2. Confirm the generated prompt no longer says "bot finding" when INCLUDE_HUMAN=true:

  bash .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr --dry-run <slug> <path> <pr>
# Inspect the generated prompt file — should say "review thread (bot or human reviewer)"

# 3. Confirm default (INCLUDE_HUMAN=false) still says "bot finding":
bash .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr --dry-run <slug> <path> <pr>
# Generated prompt should still say "bot finding"
```

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually identified circuit breaker state (`attempt_count=9, maintainer_attention=true`) for PR #3208 in Majowka/mesh-manager.
- Unblocking requires either: (a) manually resolving the GitHub review thread via GraphQL `resolveReviewThread`, or (b) resetting the scanner state file and re-dispatching a worker once the bug is fixed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a PR with a human reviewer who left a praise-only comment (not a bot).
2. Ensure `develop` branch policy requires all review threads to be resolved before merge.
3. The PR becomes merge-blocked by GitHub ("A conversation must be resolved").
4. Pulse calls `_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_preflight_remediation`, which calls `dispatch-pr` with `INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`.
5. Workers are dispatched but call `mark-blocked` (human thread, "not a bot finding").
6. After N attempts: `attempt_count` reaches escalation threshold, `maintainer_attention=true`.
7. Pulse logs "dispatch failed" indefinitely; PR stays unmerged.

## Environment

- **Latest version**: 3.32.194
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: mesh-manager (develop)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- Bug #6 was identified in local commit `2c1cb5d1c` (2026-06-06, Majowka) but was not included in upstream PR #24540 (merged 2026-06-07) which introduced `INCLUDE_HUMAN` support.
- The `INCLUDE_HUMAN` feature in PR #24540 is therefore partially broken: the scanner correctly queues human threads, but the prompt mismatch causes workers to always bail with `mark-blocked`.
- Related: `pulse-merge.sh:128` is the only production caller of `dispatch-pr` with `INCLUDE_HUMAN=true`.

title: fix(pulse): dispatch existing eligible work before cross-repo label maintenance
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Description

Pulse computes current capacity, then performs three cross-repository label-maintenance sweeps before its first worker dispatch. Live cycles with 24 available slots and two already-eligible issues spent 270-310 seconds in `preflight_capacity_and_labels` before reaching `Early dispatch_max`. A concurrent, expected setup deployment then restarted Pulse, so repeated cycles ended with zero launches even though runnable work was already visible.

The setup restart is not the defect. The defect is that already-eligible work waits behind maintenance that is only required to reveal additional label-gated work.

## Expected Behavior

After cleanup and capacity calculation, Pulse should attempt already-eligible candidates before cross-repository consolidation and simplification maintenance. Label maintenance must remain idempotent and bounded, and candidates newly unblocked by it must retain a same-cycle dispatch path.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh --window 30m --json
rg 'preflight_capacity_and_labels|substage:cap_labels|preflight_early_dispatch' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log
```

**Actual output**:

```text
workers=0/24, outcome=interrupted, consecutive_no_progress_cycles=3
substage:cap_labels/reevaluate_consolidation_labels  21s
substage:cap_labels/backfill_consolidation_labels   153s
substage:cap_labels/reevaluate_simplification_labels 116s
preflight_capacity_and_labels                       310s
```

Observed production path:

1. `_run_preflight_stages` starts merge-first and cleanup.
2. `preflight_capacity_and_labels` calculates capacity, then runs consolidation re-evaluation, consolidation backfill, and simplification re-evaluation.
3. Only after that entire group returns does `_preflight_early_dispatch` call `apply_dispatch_max`.

Measured evidence from three live cycles:

- Capacity: `workers=0/24`, with two eligible unassigned issues visible.
- Label-maintenance group durations included 247 seconds plus an incomplete simplification pass, then 310 seconds on the next complete cycle.
- Complete-cycle substages were 21 seconds for consolidation re-evaluation, 153 seconds for consolidation backfill, and 116 seconds for simplification re-evaluation.
- The dispatch log appeared only after the 310-second group completed.
- Setup stage timings independently showed an authorized deployment completing at the interruption time, confirming that SIGTERM/restart was external rather than a dispatch crash.

Causal status: confirmed ordering defect. The owning call chain is `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_run_preflight_stages` to `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh::_preflight_capacity_and_labels` to the three maintenance sweeps, followed by `_preflight_early_dispatch`.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:156-231` — separate fast capacity calculation from cross-repository label maintenance while preserving explicit returns and substage telemetry.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1384-1429` — order the first unwrapped dispatch before label maintenance and retain a same-cycle refill after maintenance.
- EDIT or NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` or a focused preflight-order test — assert the dispatch/maintenance ordering and timeout boundary.

### Complete Write Surface

- Callers/readers: `_run_preflight_stages` is the production orchestrator; `_preflight_early_dispatch` and `apply_dispatch_max` own worker launch.
- Writers/mutation paths: consolidation and simplification sweeps may edit GitHub labels/comments or create consolidation children; preserve their current idempotency and timeout behavior.
- Tests/fixtures: stage-wiring and merge-first nonblocking tests inspect static call order; add focused coverage rather than relying only on runtime logs.
- Schemas/config: no schema or user-config migration is required. Preserve `PREFLIGHT_GROUP_TIMEOUT`, `PRE_RUN_STAGE_TIMEOUT`, and `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_ASYNC_POST_DISPATCH_HOUSEKEEPING`.
- Generated/deployed mirrors: setup deploys `.agents/scripts/` into the runtime agents directory. Edit repository sources only.
- Cleanup/rollback: retain the current ordering behind a small function boundary so reverting the orchestration lines restores the previous behavior.

### Implementation Steps

1. Split capacity/session calculation from consolidation and simplification maintenance.
2. Keep merge-first and cleanup ahead of capacity.
3. Run the first `apply_dispatch_max` path after capacity and outside `run_stage_with_timeout`; per-candidate timeouts remain the safety boundary.
4. Run label maintenance under the existing bounded group timeout.
5. Preserve a same-cycle dispatch/refill after maintenance so newly cleared or backfilled work does not wait for a later cycle. Avoid duplicating routine-comment responses.
6. Add a regression test that fails if label maintenance moves ahead of the first dispatch or if worker dispatch is wrapped by the group timeout.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not place `apply_dispatch_max` inside `run_stage_with_timeout`; the group timeout previously killed candidates still within their individual budgets.
- Preserve merge-first as asynchronous and before dispatch.
- Preserve label maintenance semantics and all trust/eligibility gates; this change only reorders when existing eligible candidates are attempted.
- A setup-triggered Pulse restart remains expected. The repair reduces the vulnerable no-worker window rather than suppressing authorized restarts.
- Multiple fill passes must remain deduplicated through existing claim, assignment, ledger, and candidate gates.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With free capacity and an already-eligible candidate, the first dispatch call occurs before consolidation/simplification maintenance.
- [ ] Work newly unblocked by label maintenance still has a same-cycle dispatch path.
- [ ] Dispatch remains outside the preflight group timeout, preserving per-candidate timeout safety.
- [ ] Merge-first ordering, trust gates, deduplication, label maintenance, and routine-comment behavior do not regress.
- [ ] Focused tests, ShellCheck, and repository lint pass.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Pulse preflight starvation early dispatch` returned no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: no open or merged issue/PR matched the ordering defect; live HEAD still reproduces it.
- [x] File refs verified: production orchestrator, preflight helper, and focused tests exist at current HEAD.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` because this changes self-hosting scheduler ordering and must preserve timeout, concurrency, and mutation semantics.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped because this interactive session will implement and verify the fix directly.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The primary interactive session owns immediate implementation.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Live timing, process, setup-stage, and current-HEAD call-chain evidence captured in this session.
- **Verification run:** Unverified before implementation.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Recheck if another PR changes `_run_preflight_stages` or the maintenance function boundaries before editing.
